DCM is a leading Canadian tech-enabled provider of print and digital solutions that help simplify complex marketing communications and operations workflow. DCM serves over 2,500 clients including 70 of the 100 largest Canadian corporations and leading government agencies. Our core strength lies in delivering individualized services to our clients that simplify their communications, including customized printing, highly personalized marketing communications, campaign management, digital signage, and digital asset management. From omnichannel marketing campaigns to large-scale print and digital workflows, our goal is to make complex tasks surprisingly simple, allowing our clients to focus on what they do best.

The Role

As a Supervisor, Environmental, Health, Safety & Quality (EHSQ), you will lead the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of EHSQ systems across the organization. This role is responsible for ensuring compliance, driving continuous improvement across sites, and overseeing the ISO 9001 Quality Management System, along with supporting alignment with ISO 14001 (Environmental) and ISO 45001 (Health & Safety) frameworks.

This is a hybrid role, working a minimum of 2-3 days onsite per week. As this role will mainly be responsible for our Brampton and Burlington operations, you will be expected to split your onsite days between these two locations on a weekly basis. Collaboration across other DCM's Canadian locations, cross-functionally is also required.

Key Responsibilities

Own and maintain the ISO 9001 Quality Management System across multiple sites, ensuring compliance, audit readiness, and continuous improvement of quality processes

Manage Quality Incident Response (QIR) process and escalations and engage with customers on quality issues and corrective actions, ensuring to track and report quality KPIs and performance trends

Support internal auditor training and capability development

Maintain and improve Health & Safety Management System, ensuring compliance with Canadian legistlation

Lead incident investigations, root cause analyses, and corrective/preventive actions to improve workplace safety and reduce risk

Support injury management, ergonomic assessments and claims process and 

Monitor safety performance and recommend risk reduction initiatives

Maintain certification compliance, including FSC, MDEL, SGP, and SFI, and support audits across sites for certification requirements

Support alignment with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 best practices

Drive continuous improvement initiatives, standardize best practices across Canadian sites

Deliver training on EHSQ systems and compliance requirements

Provide reporting and insights on risk and trends to leadership and maintain business continuity and emergency response planning

Skills & Experiences

Post-secondary education in Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Quality, or related field (designation preferred), with 3–5 years working in a manufacturing or multi-site production environment 

Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001 is required, with familiarity of ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 an asset 

Understanding of Canadian health & safety and environmental regulations 

Experience supporting certification programs such as FSC, SGP, and SFI

Demonstrated experience leading incident investigations and implementing corrective actions

Knowledge of workers’ compensation and injury management 

Strong communication skills with ability to translate technical concepts to diverse audiences

Results-oriented mindset with a focus on KPIs, compliance, and continuous improvement

What we offer

Comprehensive healthcare, dental, and vision coverage for you and family

Company-matched pension program

Tuition reimbursement to invest in your growth and career development

Collaborative and supportive work environment where your ideas are valued and your impact is visible

jobs.title: Principal Consultant, Renewable Energy Land Use Planner
jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Clean Energy Development in the Pacific Northwest

ERM
is seeking a Principal Consultant, Renewable Energy Land Use Planner
in Portland, Oregon or Seattle, Washington
to help lead and expand our renewable energy permitting practice across the Pacific Northwest. In this highly visible role, you will guide complex permitting, environmental review, and land use planning efforts that support the development of utility-scale renewable energy and infrastructure projects, helping clients advance the clean energy transition while navigating regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations.

Why This Role Matters?

As renewable energy development accelerates throughout the Pacific Northwest, successful project delivery depends on thoughtful permitting strategies, regulatory expertise, and strong collaboration with agencies and stakeholders. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to clients, leading land use planning and permitting efforts that enable critical clean energy infrastructure projects to move forward efficiently and responsibly.

What Your Impact Is:

You will help clients successfully develop renewable energy and infrastructure projects by leading permitting strategies, preparing regulatory applications, evaluating land use requirements, and coordinating multidisciplinary teams. Your expertise will help identify permitting risks, develop practical solutions, and support sustainable project approvals throughout Oregon and Washington.

What You'll Bring:

Required

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Environmental Planning, Urban and Regional Planning, Environmental Science, Geography, Natural Resources, Public Policy, or a related field, or 12 years of equivalent experience.
6+ years of experience supporting permitting and land use planning efforts for renewable energy, transmission, infrastructure, or similar development projects.
Demonstrated experience preparing land use permit applications and supporting local government approval processes.
Experience conducting zoning analyses, code consistency evaluations, and preparing findings demonstrating compliance with local and state land use regulations.
Familiarity with Oregon land use planning requirements, including Oregon Statewide Planning Goals and county development codes.
Familiarity with Washington land use regulations, SEPA review processes, and local development permitting requirements.
Excellent technical writing, communication, and client management skills.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced consulting environment while managing multiple concurrent projects.
Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.

Preferred

AICP certification.
Experience working directly with Oregon and Washington counties, States (EFSC, EFSEC), planning commissions, or local hearing bodies.
Experience obtaining Oregon and Washington wetland and waters permits, including permitting under State Removal-Fill programs, Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, and related state and federal regulatory frameworks.
Experience developing wetland, waters, and habitat mitigation strategies and coordinating with state and federal resource agencies to support renewable energy, transmission, and infrastructure projects.
Knowledge of Oregon Department of State Lands (DSL), Washington Department of Ecology, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and state and federal habitat mitigation requirements preferred.

Key Responsibilities:

Lead and support the development of permit strategies and entitlement pathways for environmental permitting and land use planning efforts associated with utility-scale solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS), wind energy, transmission, and other energy infrastructure projects throughout Oregon and Washington.
Lead preparation of county and municipal land use permit applications, including Conditional Use Permits and EFSC/EFSEC applications.
Coordinate with state agencies, counties, municipalities, and special districts to support permitting and regulatory compliance requirements.
Conduct detailed zoning and land use due diligence assessments for project sites.
Interpret local development codes, comprehensive plans, and applicable state land use requirements to identify permitting risks and opportunities.
Prepare code consistency analyses demonstrating project conformance with applicable code.
Evaluate local permitting pathways and jurisdiction-specific code requirements for renewable energy developments.
Develop findings of fact and permit application narratives supporting project approvals.
Support projects undergoing review through the Oregon Energy Facility Siting Council (EFSC) and Washington Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council (EFSEC) process, including preparation of application materials, Requests for Amendment, compliance reporting, and coordination with Oregon Department of Energy staff.
Coordinate with interdisciplinary project teams including biologists, wetland scientists, archaeologists, visual resources specialists, and other technical experts regarding technical studies and review environmental documentation prepared in support of permit applications.
Mentor junior and mid-level staff in environmental permitting, land use planning, and project management.
Provide technical review and quality assurance for permitting deliverables.
Contribute to development of best practices, tools, and methodologies for renewable energy permitting projects.

For the Principal Consultant, Renewable Energy Land Use Planner
position, the anticipated annual base pay is $100,600–$152,100 (USD)
. Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off (vacation, sick, and floating holidays), parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, 401(k), and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.

Who We Are:

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

jobs.description:
U.S. Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officers diligently work to safeguard our nation’s heroes and their families from health hazards.

As a professional in the environmental science or environmental engineer field, a career as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer might be one for you.

Outstanding Benefits and Opportunities

As an Environmental Science / Engineering Officer for the U.S. Army, you will identify and evaluate potential health risks and develop a course of action to control or prevent disease, illness, and injury. You may supervise the scientific research for environmental health and industrial hygiene, assess weapons, equipment, clothing, and material systems, and develop policies, programs, and operations to ensure the health and safety of Soldiers and staff. You will attend trainings, continued education programs, seminars, and conferences to broaden your knowledge base, collaborate with other top professionals and interact with the newest technologies in the field.

If you choose to join the Army Reserve, you will be able to serve your country as needed while still supporting your community.

Regardless of how you choose to serve, a career as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer allows you to be all you can be.

Outstanding Benefits and Opportunities

When you join the Army Medical Service Corps, you’ll be making a difference in the lives of our Soldiers and the country at large while gaining access to invaluable opportunities, like supporting humanitarian missions, being part of a dedicated healthcare team, and leadership training, all while earning a competitive benefits package.

Benefits may include:
★ Repayment of qualified education loans to lending institution, paid annually over a maximum of 3 years while serving
★ Based on your field of concentration, you may be eligible for an accession bonus
★ Travel opportunities within the United States and abroad
★ Up to 30 days of paid vacation earned annually
★ Enrollment into the Uniformed Services Blended Retirement System
★ No- to low-cost medical and dental care for you and your family
★ Commissary and post exchange shopping privileges
★ Specialized training to become a leader in medicine

Eligibility Requirements

★ Must have a bachelor’s degree from an educational program accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health with a major in a public-health-relevant field or a bachelor’s degree from a program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology with a major in an environmental engineering-relevant field
★ Must be a U.S. citizen to serve Active Duty
★ Must have a permanent U.S. residency for Army Reserve

Have questions or want more information?

To find out more information about becoming an Environmental Science / Engineering Officer in the U.S. Army, visit www.goarmy.com/medicine. You may also contact your local Army Healthcare Recruiter to learn how you can get started on your journey as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer.

jobs.title: Environmental Professional III
jobs.description:
#WeAreONEOK
– Fortune 500 company. 100+ years in business. Leading midstream service provider. Safety first. Sustainable operations. Environmentally responsible. Employee focused.

Job Summary

Role focus is on environmental support of construction and maintenance efforts with significant work within natural and cultural resource compliance. Major work activities include but are not limited to: desktop analysis, permit applicability review, agency interactions, management of 3rd party resource experts, construction compliance planning, field compliance inspections, project restoration, and close out requirements. Job Profile Summary

Responsible for coordinating environmental compliance, remediation and company support for operating segments and construction projects through the application of knowledge and experience of compliance and environmental programs in accordance with the company mission, vision, and values.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Provide mentoring to entry level employees on compliance system management, assisting with compliance requirements and organizational procedures and tools.
Develop tools and templates to manage the collection of environmental compliance and remediation information that results in enhanced compliance and company performance with the appropriate quality and accuracy reviews of the data.
Manage field inspections for operating assets and construction projects. Provide senior level knowledge of compliance requirements and operating or construction parameters to answer questions regarding applicability and compliance requirements.
Enhance existing compliance programs based on audit results. Lead internal audits of facilities within and outside areas of responsibility.
Represent the company in the evaluation and implementation of minor emerging regulatory issues through committees of state based Industry Associations or in support of the company's Regulatory Issue Guideline.
Recognize and resolve regulatory applicability issues and identify compliance requirements and tasks. Able to apply risk based analysis of compliance related to operations or construction practices. Provide support to less experienced professionals to resolve complex questions of applicability or requirements.
Capable of managing all environmental programs and their application within a complex operating asset or construction projects.
Recognize the need for and development of new procedures and tools to facilitate and demonstrate compliance.
Review environmental inspection reports and resolve potential compliance issues based on knowledge of regulations, construction practices and operating assets.
Negotiate with contract and consultant resources to ensure an appropriate level of service and competitive rates for service are in place. Evaluate contractor and consultant performance and make recommendations on continued use.
Manage the permit process from start to finish for all media, including applications for new construction and operating assets. Ensure quality and accuracy of practical permit conditions based on evaluation of compliance risk.
Manage multiple compliance systems across multiple media for complex operating sites and projects. Contribute to system enhancements to improve compliance performance. Train new users on compliance systems and procedures. Participate in the development and implementation of new compliance systems.
Manage and participate in agency inspections and represent the company in negotiations on compliance or enforcement issues. Effectively represent the company operating parameters and construction practices and the applicability of environmental regulations along with rationale for compliance positions taken by the organization.
Coordinate and facilitate environmental project permitting prior to, during, and after construction for maintenance, growth and large capital projects.
Collect and review environmental field samples (air, water, and waste) for analysis.

Education

Bachelor's Degree in environmental, natural science, engineering preferred and/or a combination of formal education and the following job related experience:

Work Experience

This role is typically attained through 6 -10 years related experience in environmental compliance.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of: state and federal environmental regulations and standards and their applicability to operations.
Ability to: analyze, research, compile, and prepare permit applications, logs, reports, and correspondence and company responses to agency requests.
Ability to: evaluate, research, and interpret governmental regulations, equipment performance manuals, regulatory agency guidance and instructions, reports, correspondence, and company policies and procedures.
Ability to: pay attention to details.
Ability to: apply math, algebraic formulas, and statistics.
Ability to: interact, advise and communicate effectively, exchange information/provide instructions, conduct verbal presentations.
Ability to: develop communications utilizing fundamental technical writing skills.
Ability to: present training materials.
Ability to: utilize office equipment including computers and applicable job related software, including Microsoft Office tools.
Ability to: operate tools/equipment.

None required

Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Project Scientist for Emergency Response Team
jobs.description:
Description

At Weston Solutions, Inc. you will do meaningful work and make valuable contributions. Employee ownership at Weston is a path to professional growth and access to diverse opportunities in a highly connected community that works together across key service areas to make a difference in the environment. Weston has continued to evolve and adapt to our changing world as a premier provider of environmental and infrastructure services for over sixty years. In both the public and private sectors our teams help identify, solve, mitigate, and manage critical environmental issues to help clients achieve a more sustainable future.

Weston is hiring a Senior Project Scientist to support environmental investigation, remediation, and emergency response projects that protect public health and the environment. This role is ideal for an experienced technical leader who can manage complex field efforts, guide technical decisions, and deliver high-quality client outcomes.

This position supports a critical project with work expected to begin soon. Weston is proactively interviewing to prepare for onboarding as project activities ramp up. Start timing will align with project kickoff and mobilization schedules.

Location: Pittsburgh, PA

Key Responsibilities

Lead complex environmental investigations, remediation programs, emergency response activities, and related field and office assignments from planning through completion.
Manage project execution in accordance with scope, budget, schedule, technical requirements, regulatory standards, Weston procedures, and client expectations.
Plan and oversee field investigations and sampling programs at active construction, remediation, and potentially hazardous sites.
Direct field staff, subcontractors, and multidisciplinary teams while coordinating resources and reinforcing safe, efficient work practices.
Analyze field observations, analytical data, and monitoring results to develop defensible conclusions, recommendations, and project strategies.
Prepare and review scientific reports, investigation summaries, removal action documentation, technical memoranda, work plans, sampling plans, health and safety plans, quality assurance documents, schedules, budgets, and other deliverables.
Conduct peer reviews of project scopes, technical documents, calculations, data interpretations, and deliverables to support quality and consistency.
Identify project risks, constraints, and opportunities, and implement corrective actions when needed.
Communicate project objectives, progress, needs, concerns, and deliverable expectations to clients, stakeholders, Project Managers, subcontractors, technical teams, and leadership.
Maintain accurate and auditable field documentation, correspondence, notebooks, technical files, and project records.
Mentor junior staff and provide technical guidance to project teams.
Evaluate new technologies, tools, and techniques for potential use in project execution and Weston service offerings.

Safety Responsibilities

Lead EHS compliance for complex assignments and ensure work aligns with Weston’s EHS Program, project safety plans, technical procedures, quality requirements, and applicable regulations.
Reinforce Stop Work Authority, personal accountability, and project- and site-specific safety expectations with staff and subcontractors.
Coordinate with EHS personnel when plans do not align with project scope or site conditions.
Work safely at active and potentially hazardous sites using required PPE, including OSHA Levels D through A, as applicable.

Required Qualifications:

10 to 15 years of relevant experience in environmental investigations, remediation, emergency response operations, or a combination of these areas.
This position requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in environmental science, Geoscience, Engineering, Physical Science, Life Science, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading complex environmental site investigations or remediation projects involving potentially hazardous substances.
Ability to serve as a technical resource, guide complex technical decisions, solve problems, and manage multiple priorities.
Experience managing field operations, subcontractors, multidisciplinary teams, project scope, schedules, budgets, resources, risks, and technical deliverables.
Experience developing and reviewing technical reports, investigation documents, work plans, field sampling plans, health and safety plans, technical procedures, and quality assurance documentation.
Strong ability to analyze, interpret, organize, and communicate analytical data, monitoring results, and field observations.
Strong leadership, mentoring, client-facing, written, and verbal communication skills.
Experience using field sampling equipment, air and water monitoring instruments, PPE, and related field tools.
Valid driver’s license.

Preferred Qualifications

Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910, or willingness to obtain it.
Incident Command System training or emergency response experience.
Experience with QAPPs or UFP QAPPs.
Membership in a relevant professional organization.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and standard business communication tools.

Travel, On-Call, and Physical Requirements

Willingness to travel, complete extended field assignments, and mobilize rapidly for project or emergency response needs.
Ability to participate in on-call rotations and support 24/7 responses to environmental incidents, including chemical and oil spills.
Ability to work outdoors at active construction, investigation, and remediation sites.
Ability to walk long distances over varied terrain, climb ladders, work at elevation, and lift and carry up to 50 pounds, including field equipment and PPE.

We fully invest in our people. Weston provides a generous, comprehensive benefits package program that offers employees high value options with solid financial protection, meeting the personal needs of its people and their families.

Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K with base and matching employer stock contributions.
Paid time off including personal, holiday, and parental leave.
Life and disability plans.
Critical illness and accident plans.
Work/Life flexibility.
Professional development opportunities.

Compensation will vary based upon experience, education, skill level, and other compensable factors.

jobs.title: Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager American Peat Technology (APT) is seeking a Quality, Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Manager to lead and maintain our quality control, product regulatory compliance, environmental permitting, and product registration programs.
This is a hands-on, technical position supporting APT’s manufacturing of granular peat products, microbial inoculants, turf products, fertilizers, soil amendments, and other agricultural products sold throughout the United States and Canada.
The position combines laboratory testing, manufacturing quality control, regulatory affairs, environmental compliance, product registrations, and new product commercialization. This individual will have significant ownership and authority for APT’s quality, regulatory, and environmental compliance programs and will directly supervise the Lab Manager.
The position works closely with R&D, Production, Sales, the Safety Coordinator, management, regulatory agencies, consultants, outside laboratories, and other internal and external partners.
Key Responsibilities Quality Control & Product Quality

Lead and maintain APT’s quality-control program, including testing methods, product specifications, acceptance standards, and finished-product release criteria.
Oversee quality testing of raw materials, in-process materials, and finished products, including applicable moisture, particle size, bulk density, pH, ash, nutrient, microbial, heavy metals, and other product testing.
Provide direction and oversight to the Lab Manager and support effective laboratory operations, documentation, equipment, training, and testing priorities.
Evaluate testing data, investigate unexpected results and nonconformances, and coordinate corrective actions.
Exercise appropriate authority to hold or prevent the release of materials or products that do not meet established quality requirements.

Product Regulatory Affairs & Registrations

Own and maintain APT’s product registration program for products sold throughout the United States and Canada.
Research and interpret requirements for fertilizers, soil amendments, microbial and biological products, turf products, and other agricultural products.
Manage registrations, renewals, amendments, fees, reports, and required supporting documentation.
Review product labels, claims, guaranteed analyses, and supporting materials for regulatory compliance.
Monitor regulatory changes and coordinate responses to regulatory agency questions and requests.

Environmental Permitting & Compliance

Own environmental compliance for APT’s Minnesota manufacturing operations, including applicable state and federal permits and regulatory requirements.
Prepare and coordinate permit applications, renewals, modifications, reports, monitoring information, and other required documentation.
Monitor operations for compliance and maintain accurate, audit-ready records.
Serve as a primary contact for environmental regulatory agencies and coordinate with outside consultants and technical resources.
Support regulatory inspections, audits, investigations, and corrective actions.

New Product Development & Commercialization

Partner with R&D, Sales, Production, and other departments to identify regulatory, registration, labeling, testing, and quality requirements for new products.
Establish product specifications, QC requirements, acceptance standards, and finished-product release criteria.
Coordinate required product registrations and approvals prior to commercial sale.
Review proposed labels, claims, formulations, raw materials, and product or process changes for regulatory and quality impacts.
Maintain and continuously improve APT’s regulatory and quality-control commercialization sign-off process.

What We’re Looking For Associate degree in a scientific, technical, environmental, agricultural, microbiological, chemistry, or related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience.
Previous experience in quality control, manufacturing, environmental compliance, regulatory affairs, laboratory operations, or a related technical field preferred.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and technical reasoning skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to independently research, interpret, and apply technical procedures and regulatory requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external partners.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn applicable laboratory, quality, regulatory, and business systems.
Experience with agricultural product registrations, microbiology, qPCR, product labeling, laboratory method development, or manufacturing process improvement is preferred.

Core Competencies We are looking for someone who demonstrates attention to detail, analytical thinking, problem solving, ownership and accountability, people leadership, organization and planning, sound judgment, effective communication, collaboration, and emotional intelligence.
Schedule & Location This position is generally Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with occasional additional days or hours as needed.
Work locations include APT’s main plant in Spencer Township, APT2, and the Applied Research Center in Aitkin, Minnesota.
This position reports to the VP of Business Development and works closely with other members of the R&D team.
Benefits APT offers:
Paid time off (PTO)
Medical, dental and vision plans
Matching 401(k)
Life Insurance
Paid volunteer opportunities

Work Environment This position works across office, laboratory, manufacturing, and production environments. Responsibilities include laboratory and computer-based work as well as movement throughout manufacturing and production areas.
The position may involve exposure to laboratory chemicals, biological or microbial materials, agricultural products, fertilizers, peat, dust, odors, varying temperatures, moving equipment, and moderate to high noise levels. Appropriate PPE is required.
The position requires the ability to occasionally lift or move materials, samples, equipment, and supplies weighing up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Engineering Manager, Air Programs
jobs.description:
The Simplot Company is a diverse, privately held global food and agriculture company headquartered in Boise, Idaho. We are a true farm-to-table company with an integrated portfolio including food processing and food brands, phosphate mining, fertilizer manufacturing, farming, ranching and cattle production, and other enterprises related to agriculture.

Summary

The Senior Air Program/Engineering Environmental Manager is responsible for leading company-wide Clean Air Act (CAA) permitting and compliance programs across Simplot's diverse operations. This position serves as the Company's primary technical expert for air quality permitting, regulatory strategy, agency engagement, and air compliance assurance. About FIU

Florida International University is a Top 50, preeminent public research university with 55,000 students from all 50 states and more than 140 countries, as well as an alumni network of more than 340,000. Located in the global city of Miami, the university offers more than 200 degree programs at the undergraduate, graduate and professional levels, including medicine and law. FIU faculty are leaders in their fields and include National Academy members, Fulbright Scholars and MacArthur Genius Fellows. A Carnegie R1 institution, FIU drives impactful research in environmental resilience, health and technology and innovation. Home to the Wall of Wind and Institute of Environment, FIU stands at the forefront of discovery and innovation. With a focus on student success, economic mobility and community engagement, FIU is redefining what it means to be a public research university.

Job Information

Tenure Track Assistant Professor and Associate Professor in Environmental Health Sciences

The Robert Stempel College Of Public Health & Social Work At Florida International University (FIU) Invites Applications For Two Full-time, Tenure-earning/tenure-track Faculty Positions In The Department Of Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) Under Two Main Concentrations:

Assistant Professor (Tenure Track) ' Environmental Health Sciences (EHS)
Assistant/Associate Professor (Tenure Track or Tenured) ' Brain, Behavior, and the Environment (BBE)

FIU's Stempel College School of Public Health is ranked 36th among all public universities nationwide (U.S. News & World Report). Maintaining an active, externally funded research program

Advancing the mission to expand knowledge of how environmental pollutants impact chronic disease and population health

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about research in marine ecology, fisheries management or the socioeconomics of fisheries? Are you equally passionate about the latest developments in geospatial mapping and analysis techniques? If so, we have an exciting 12 month fixed-term (maternity cover) opportunity for you!

The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) is seeking to improve sustainable fishing practices worldwide through its eco-labelling program. Our Research Team, part of the Science and Standards Department, applies diverse analytic methods to understand MSC's impact on fish stocks, fisheries, and stakeholders.

This role offers the chance to build and analyse geospatial datasets for research directly relevant to global fisheries issues, within a professional yet informal work environment alongside a team of enthusiastic scientists. This 12-month fixed-term opportunity is best suited as a postdoctoral position or for a candidate with equivalent independent research experience.

We're looking for a data scientist experienced in geospatial software (e.g., QGIS), ready to take a leading role in analysing geospatial data, quality-assuring the MSC spatial database, and disseminating research to internal and external audiences.

You'll bring hands-on experience with geo-referenced spatial data and software platforms, strong quantitative analysis skills, and a track record of leading or contributing to writing peer-reviewed papers.

Familiarity with the MSC certification process, fisheries management, or marine fish stocks would be a bonus. Strong organisational skills, the ability to work independently, and good communication skills in a multi-national, multi-disciplinary team round out what we're looking for.
If this has inspired you, please apply here by submitting your CV and a covering letter. We look forward to hearing from you!

Important information

We’re an international organisation and our employees all demonstrate a level of cultural awareness, and value the diverse views and approaches relevant to the MSC program.
The MSC is committed to flexible working. The successful candidate will need to work from the London, UK office for a minimum of 50% of their working time each month. The remaining time can be worked from home. During the onboarding process, hybrid work may require more in-office work than remote work.

Please be aware, we are only able to progress with candidates
who already have the right to work in the location specified in this advert. Unfortunately, we are not able to offer visa sponsorship at this time.

The MSC is committed to the principles of equality and fairness and we welcome applications from all communities. We do not discriminate on the grounds of age, ethnicity, race, colour, religion or belief, gender or gender identity, sexual orientation or disability. If you consider yourself to have a disability and need reasonable adjustments made during the recruitment and selection process, please let us know how we can help you.

Working at the MSC

The MSC’s vision is for the world’s oceans to be teeming with life, and seafood supplies safeguarded for this and future generations. Today, the impacts of overfishing and climate change pose an even greater threat to the ocean and fish stocks. Through our internationally recognised certification and ecolabeling program, well-managed sustainable fisheries are recognised and rewarded throughout the seafood supply chain. Over 700 fisheries around the world, representing 19% of the annual global marine catch, are now engaged in the MSC program and MSC certified and labelled seafood products are now available in over 66 countries. Through partnerships and collective endeavour, we are on a mission to end overfishing.

Conduct PID tuning and flight-controller parameter optimization
for stable, responsive, and efficient flight performance.
Analyse flight logs, telemetry, and flight behaviour to identify issues and recommend corrective actions.
Validate new hardware, avionics, sensors, payloads, communication systems, and software/firmware releases through flight testing.
Diagnose flight behaviour and provide detailed technical feedback to engineering teams.
Evaluate and troubleshoot sensors, communication systems, antennas, batteries, and flight controllers
during flight testing.

.

.

, including situations where visual or GPS-based navigation is unavailable.
Demonstrated experience or strong practical capability in long-range flying without GPS
/ GPS-denied flight conditions.
Strong understanding of PID tuning
, including practical experience tuning PID parameters for flight stability, responsiveness, and control.
Strong knowledge of different flight controllers
, their configurations, parameters, and practical application in UAVs.
Good understanding of sensors used in UAVs
, including their role in flight control, navigation, and stabilization, and ability to troubleshoot sensor-related issues.
Good understanding of UAV communication systems
, telemetry, RC links, communication loss, and associated failsafe mechanisms.
Strong understanding of antenna types, antenna theory, placement, orientation, and their impact on UAV communication/range
.
Practical understanding of UAV battery configurations
, battery selection, voltage/current requirements, power systems, and their impact on aircraft performance and endurance.
Proven capability to recover aircraft from: GPS failures, Compass failures, Sensor malfunctions, Communication loss, Flight-controller abnormalities, Stall or unstable flight conditions
Strong understanding of fixed-wing aerodynamics and flight dynamics.
Experience with flight-log analysis, preferably ArduPilot/PX4 logs
.
Ability to identify root causes of flight issues using telemetry, logs, and observed flight behaviour.
Excellent troubleshooting and decision-making skills under pressure.

.
Knowledge of Mission Planner and QGroundControl
.

Local candidate with good knowledge of nearby flying locations and terrain.

Asbestos and hazardous building materials

Working outdoors conducting fieldwork supporting subsurface exploration in varying weather conditions
Walking over rough, uneven terrain and standing for potentially up to 12 hours a day
Routinely lifting and carrying 40-50lbs (field/laboratory samples and equipment)
Maneuvering field equipment safely, such as a loaded wheelbarrow, on uneven ground around active construction sites

jobs.title: Senior Advisor, Environmental Risk Management and Site Remediation
jobs.description:
At Alto, we are actively contributing to the transformation of Canada's future with our high-speed train project connecting Quebec City and Toronto. With the support of the Government of Canada, this innovative project aims to improve the quality of life of our citizens, strengthen ties between communities and stimulate economic growth.

Would you like to take on a stimulating, high-impact challenge? We are looking for a Senior Advisor, Environmental Risk Management and Site Remediation.

Please note that the candidate may be based in one of our 4 offices: Montreal, Quebec City, Toronto or Ottawa.

The role

Reporting to the Director, Impact Assessment, the incumbent provides expertise in environmental risk management and contaminated site remediation to support, among other things, the real estate team in property acquisitions and asset management, the environmental team in identifying risks and managing environmental impacts, and the construction team in developing and implementing soil management plans. The incumbent contributes to the development and implementation of processes, programs, and plans aimed at ensuring compliance with environmental risk management requirements and corporate policies. The role also provides guidance on the application of compliance requirements, plans and oversees environmental site assessments, and supports land managers in their activities.

The Responsibilities

Risk management

Identify, or contribute to the identification of, environmental and financial risks, and ensure due diligence throughout asset acquisition and management processes.
Develop operational processes and an environmental risk management program related to real estate assets that support project delivery while meeting the standards required for a major linear infrastructure project.
Understand and define a framework of requirements applicable to Alto as a federal Crown corporation.
Plan, coordinate, and oversee the completion of environmental site assessments for the Project.

Collaboration, coordination and communication

Provide technical and strategic advice to the real estate management, design, construction, and operations teams regarding the implementation of mitigation measures and sustainable solutions related to soil and groundwater management.
Collaborate with internal project teams and the private development partner (PDP) to ensure the planning of all required work and the monitoring of ongoing mandates and schedules.
Liaise with external stakeholders and partners, including regulatory agencies, communities, insurers, specialized consultants, and environmental partners.
Prepare and review technical reports, plans and specifications, and support related communications.
Oversee the preparation of environmental management plans for soil and groundwater during the Project’s construction and operational phases.
Contribute to the planning of consultation and engagement activities and participate in the Project’s public consultation processes.
Support the development of the Project’s environmental communications related to environmental risks associated with land and property management.

Strategic monitoring

Monitor evolving regulations and societal expectations regarding the management and remediation of contaminated sites.
Stay informed of emerging innovations and recognized industry practices.

The Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Studies, Engineering, Science, or a related field.
Master’s degree in Management or Environmental Studies (asset).
10 to 15 years of experience in a similar role.
Strong knowledge of federal and provincial laws, regulations, policies, and guidelines related to contaminated sites (Quebec and Ontario).
Experience with large-scale projects and/or the management of significant real estate asset portfolios.
Experience managing environmental programs.
Experience in environmental site assessments, risk analysis, incident reporting, soil and groundwater management during construction activities, and contaminated site remediation.
Ability to build and maintain trusted relationships internally and with external partners.
Demonstrated ability to engage and mobilize stakeholders around common objectives.
Results-oriented, with the ability to maintain focus despite challenges or constraints.
Ability to develop practical, fit-for-purpose solutions that take operational and regulatory realities into account.
Strong active listening and collaboration skills.
Bilingualism (French and English), both spoken and written.
Assets: Knowledge of linear infrastructure projects, railway or transportation industry experience, and versatility.

Why join our innovative team?

Basic paid group insurance for you and your family: medical, dental, life, disability, etc.
Access to wellness and health accounts to support your lifestyle.
Flex-Alto account of $500 to encourage a healthier approach and a more sustainable mode of transportation.
A retirement plan and savings options (RRSP and TFSA).
Vacations based on experience, available upon hiring.
An incentive compensation program.
Flexible hybrid work mode.
A work environment that encourages initiative, innovation, and forward-thinking solutions.
A unique opportunity to shape the future of transportation in Canada.

We work to create high-performance, diversified teams

At Alto, we believe in the power of diverse teams. We aspire to provide an inclusive and equitable work environment where everyone can develop and flourish. Alto offers equal employment opportunities to all and invites qualified individuals, regardless of their identity, origin or situation, to apply.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking a GIS Specialist to make complex field information useful for federal facility assessment and hurricane recovery work in Kauai, Hawaii. Engineering teams may inspect damaged roofs and buildings, assess utilities and access routes, and define immediate repairs across multiple locations. You will turn inspection findings, photos, asset records, and field coordinates into maps and spatial data that show where damage occurred and what work remains. Your products will support the initial assessment report, help teams plan access and repair priorities, and give project leaders a clearer picture as conditions change.

This role will require an onsite presence in Kauai, Hawaii and is eligible for per diem related expenses when appropriate.

Key Responsibilities
Create and maintain GIS maps, geodatabases, dashboards, and spatial datasets for facilities and infrastructure.
Integrate field survey information, photographs, inspection findings, and asset records into consistent GIS products.
Support mobile data collection and establish quality control procedures for field updates.
Prepare maps and exhibits for assessment reports, repair plans, site access, and construction coordination.
Analyze spatial data to identify affected facilities, utility corridors, access routes, and repair priorities.
Coordinate with engineers, construction managers, and field teams to resolve data gaps and maintain accurate records.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in geography, geographic information systems, geospatial science, engineering, or a related field and 4+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

8+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects.
Experience with Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, Field Maps, or Survey123.
Experience with federal facility mapping, utility systems, or post event damage assessments.

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $65000 to $95000.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking a GIS Specialist to make complex field information useful for federal facility assessment and hurricane recovery work in Kauai, Hawaii. Engineering teams may inspect damaged roofs and buildings, assess utilities and access routes, and define immediate repairs across multiple locations. You will turn inspection findings, photos, asset records, and field coordinates into maps and spatial data that show where damage occurred and what work remains. Your products will support the initial assessment report, help teams plan access and repair priorities, and give project leaders a clearer picture as conditions change.

This role will require an onsite presence in Kauai, Hawaii and is eligible for per diem related expenses when appropriate.

Key Responsibilities
Create and maintain GIS maps, geodatabases, dashboards, and spatial datasets for facilities and infrastructure.
Integrate field survey information, photographs, inspection findings, and asset records into consistent GIS products.
Support mobile data collection and establish quality control procedures for field updates.
Prepare maps and exhibits for assessment reports, repair plans, site access, and construction coordination.
Analyze spatial data to identify affected facilities, utility corridors, access routes, and repair priorities.
Coordinate with engineers, construction managers, and field teams to resolve data gaps and maintain accurate records.

Bachelor’s degree in geography, geographic information systems, geospatial science, engineering, or a related field and 4+ years of GIS mapping and spatial data management for infrastructure, facilities, or construction projects or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.

Experience with federal facility mapping, utility systems, or post event damage assessments.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Senior Rehabilitation Biologist

Posting Date:
August 2026

Job Department: Animal Rescue

Schedule:
Full Time

Job Type:
On-site

Location:
National Aquarium Pier 3 501 E Pratt St Baltimore, MD 21202/ACRC 901 E. Fayette St Baltimore, MD 21202/6405 Seabay Drive, Bldg #2600, Ocean City, MD 21842

Job Summary

The National Aquarium is seeking a Senior Rehabilitation Biologist responsible for executing complex, professional work for all aspects of animal husbandry and welfare within the Animal Rescue department, including stranding response and rehabilitation of sea turtles. Specifically, this includes the design, set-up, care and maintenance of habitats, disease recognition and medical treatment, life support system construction and operation, field work, species identification and knowledge, and incident response. In addition to the Senior Rehabilitation Biologist’s scheduled duties, the incumbent is expected to use independent judgment and critical thinking to problem solve, keeping human and animal welfare at the forefront of decision making and actions. Responsible for being able to lead special projects and other investigations aimed at furthering the quality of animal care and welfare. The Senior Rehabilitation Biologist position may also be responsible to serve as the main point of contact for the area(s) to which they are assigned, or as a liaison cross-departmentally within the Aquarium or with external agencies (NOAA & USFWS). May supervise, train and mentor paid husbandry staff and volunteers.

Key Requirements

Performs general daily husbandry and medical treatment functions including the maintenance of habitats and quarantine facilities at a high level of quality as defined in our protocols; does so without direct supervision.
Performs the duties and maintains the skills of a Rehabilitation Biologist.
Directly responsible for advanced husbandry duties such as animal quarantine protocols, habitat design, leading field work, record keeping, acquisition/disposition, and leading triage and transport of animals.
May supervise, train and mentor paid husbandry staff and volunteers in the development of job and leadership skills relating to general husbandry and medical functions, habitat design, construction and maintenance, project management, and field techniques.
Assumes responsibility for the implementation of daily operations, emergency response, and effective teamwork within their husbandry area, as scheduled.
As scheduled, provide 24-hour coverage of Stranding Hotline, and provide exemplary customer service.
Work cooperatively with Animal Health to manage and execute the Aquarium’s regional response to live-stranded sea turtles according to established protocols.
Contributes to the development or refinement of policies and procedures relating to essential functions of the assigned section, as directed. Policies and procedures may cross more than one department/ assigned section.
Implement Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s) and Incident Action Plans (IAP’s) related to stranding response, manage events under the Incident Command System, and ensure staff and animal safety.
Provides operational and logistical support to stranding events, and as requested by Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
Maintain life support systems.
Develop and manage research goals for sea turtles in rehabilitation.
Collaborate with Director on Animal Rescue Protocols to review and update.
Must have specialized knowledge about sea turtle and/or marine mammal biology and have an affinity for wild animals, including a reasonable comfort level around large and/or aggressive animals.
Comprehensive knowledge of and ability to set up laboratory and diagnostic testing, animal medical treatment methods, and pharmacology and drug dosing as prescribed by veterinarian(s); must be familiar with quarantine protocols.
Familiarity with computers is necessary, including MS Office software (Word/Excel/Teams), Zoom, and Adobe; ability to learn & effectively use all proprietary Aquarium software.
Expected to act as a role model within and beyond the division; must professionally demonstrate good judgment and communication skills through interpersonal effectiveness and fostering a learning culture.
Promote teamwork and a positive and productive work environment.
Accountable to use independent judgment and critical thinking to problem solve, keeping human safety and animal welfare at the forefront of decision making and actions. Innovation may be required to temporarily modify existing policies and procedures. Problems to solve are typically within the assigned section.
Willingness and ability to mentor new staff, volunteers, and interns while exhibiting the same or higher levels of technical skill/knowledge.
Stays abreast of current trends in the related field to ensure that National Aquarium programs, policies, and protocols continue to evolve and improve.
Support company mission.
Adhere to all organizational and departmental policies and procedures.
Other duties as assigned or required.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in aquatic sciences, environmental or related science or equivalent experience.
Minimum of three years of previous professional work experience with rehabilitation, and or stranding response organization with preference to those with experience with both pinnipeds and sea turtles.
Ability to be certified in the operation of an electric pallet jack/stacker and overhead crane.
Ability and willingness to work a flexible schedule including weekends, holidays and occasional evenings.
Employees assigned to this position will be required to possess and maintain a valid and current motor vehicle operator’s license, have an acceptable driving record, and possess the ability to drive a variety of vehicles (cars, vans/trucks).
Ability to climb ladders, lift and carry 50 lbs, and physically restrain large, wild animals.

Preferred

Previous experience mentoring or training staff, interns or volunteers.
Veterinary Technician experience or license.
CPR/AED and basic First-Aid Certification
24hr HAZWOPER Certification.
Familiarity with electronic animal record keeping software systems (i.e. Tracks, ZIMS, etc.)
Previous experience responding to hotline calls and field stranding response.
Ability to pass a Department of Transportation medical exam.

Total Compensation Information

Salary range ($58,660-71,399 annual).
National Aquarium provides an excellent benefits package, including four weeks paid time off, and six paid floating holidays and up to four weeks of paid family leave. Employees are eligible for health care (single and family) after 30 days of full-time work. Conservation day leave and 401(k) plan with employer match available.

About The National Aquarium

Established in 1981, the National Aquarium in Baltimore, Maryland, is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to connect people with nature to inspire compassion and care for our ocean planet. The Aquarium’s award-winning habitats are home to thousands of animals representing hundreds of species of fish, birds, amphibians, reptiles and mammals. We are proud to be accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA) and exceed industry standards in all aspects of animal care and welfare.

More than 1.2 million people visit the Aquarium each year to experience our immersive exhibits, and we reach far more through our science-based education programs and hands-on field conservation work. The National Aquarium is one of the top three aquariums in the United States and the largest paid cultural attraction in Maryland.

Our Mission and Goals

The Aquarium’s mission—to connect people with nature to inspire compassion and care for our ocean planet—begins within the walls of its buildings, but it does not end there. The Aquarium protects, enhances and restores natural resources through education and engagement, habitat restoration, animal rescue and sustainable business practices, with its conservation work guided by three overarching goals—to combat climate change, save wildlife and habitats, and stop plastic pollution.

Our Values

At the National Aquarium, our core values form the basis for our beliefs about our organization, our colleagues and ourselves, and serve as the framework to guide our behaviors and actions to achieve our mission.

Connection:
We take the time to build lasting connections with each other, our guests, the animals in our care and the nature that surrounds us. We communicate clearly and collaborate readily within and across teams. We engage thoughtfully with our partners. We practice shared accountability.

Curiosity:
We center learning and growth in all that we do. Our people are empowered to explore new approaches. We support taking risks. We value diverse perspectives and bold ideas. We embrace change.

Optimism
: We celebrate the power of positive moments and shared experiences. We seek out opportunities to have fun. We reconnect with our purpose through sharing successes with our colleagues.

Service:
We are in service to each other, our guests and our communities. We make intentional decisions and actions for the benefit of the people and animals within our organization.

Wellbeing:
We ensure our people and animals have what they need mentally and physically to thrive. We are committed to improving the wellbeing of communities and sharing the healing power of natural for all.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Justice

National Aquarium values an inclusive and diverse environment for all employees, volunteers, and interns. Our goal is to recruit, develop, and retain the most talented people from a candidate pool representative of the variety of communities we serve. With a commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice, the Aquarium is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and promotes an environment free from all discrimination and harassment.

In the selection and retention of employees, volunteers, and interns, we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or belief, national, social, or ethnic origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age, physical, mental, or sensory disability, sex (including pregnancy or childbirth), marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, arrest record, family or caregiver status, HIV status, socioeconomic status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Our organization is dedicated to this policy with respect to all terms and conditions of employment, including but not limited to recruitment, training, promotions, performance management, and separation, and general treatment during time of employment.

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step Into Your New Role

Kleinfelder is currently seeking an experienced Ecologist/Environmental Scientist to join our Tampa, FL office.

Working as part of a team, the successful candidate will assist with ecological field assessments for projects in the mining, energy, and commercial development industries. Primary tasks will include protected species surveys, gopher tortoise relocations, vegetative monitoring, hydrologic monitoring, water quality sampling and support with other ecological assessments, as well as reporting. The ideal candidate should have knowledge of the natural resources of Florida and a minimum of 3 years of applicable job experience.

Candidate should also possess strong time management, problem solving, communication, organizational skills, and have relevant computer/software experience. This position requires solid technical writing and verbal communication skills, including coordination with team members and project managers, as well as periodically with clients and regulatory agency staff.

Candidate must be a Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) Gopher Tortoise Authorized Agent (AA) for mechanical excavation.

Candidate will be required to go through and obtain an MSHA New Miner Training certificate as part of on-the-job training.

This position is anticipated to be 80% field work/20% office work. Travel (local/overnight) may account for up to 30%.

The ability to travel, both within Florida and nationwide, and a clear driving record are also required. Potential candidates should be able to work effectively in both team environments and with limited supervision. Candidates should have availability to work outside of typical business hours. Flexibility in daily work schedule and willingness to work long hours in adverse environmental conditions and in remote areas is required.

Qualifications:

A bachelor's degree in natural resources (i.e. biological, zoology, botany, ecology or environmental science).
Experience conducting threatened and endangered species surveys per FWC and United States Fish and Wildlife Service survey protocols/guidelines.
Ability to lead gopher tortoise relocation efforts including mechanical excavation and bucket trapping.
Minimum of 3 years of experience as a natural resources professional is required.
Proficiency in use of ESRI Field maps, a sub-meter GPS and data processing is also desired.
Experience operating a 4x4 truck preferred.

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

Move Forward with Kleinfelder:
 Kleinfelder and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, has been connecting great people to the best work since 1961. We are engineers, scientists, and construction professionals providing solutions that improve our clients’ transportation, water, energy, and other private infrastructure. As a responsive, cross-disciplinary team of bright, curious, and innovative problem-solvers, we are dedicated to doing the right thing, every day, on every project from over 110 offices in the US, Canada, and Australia. Connecting great people to the best work is our purpose – together, we deliver. 

Progress with an Employer that Values You

We are a stronger organization when we are a diverse workforce and believe that through diversity, equity, and inclusion comes creativity, innovation, and unity. We are proud to offer the following: 

Benefits:

We support these efforts through reimbursements for continuing education as well as many of the expenses associated with trainings and certifications, and opportunities for career development through our internal Mentoring Program. 

Equal Opportunity:

Environmental Specialist – Stack/Emissions Testing Technician

Sanders Engineering and Analytical Services, Inc. (SEAS) | Mobile, AL | Full-Time, On-Site

Pay: $45,000 – $50,000 per year for entry level. Pay negotiable with prior experience.

 Travel: 50%

About SEAS

Since 1978, Sanders Engineering and Analytical Services has performed thousands of air emissions tests for industrial clients using EPA test methods. Based in Mobile, Alabama, we provide state and federal compliance testing and design custom test programs to meet each client's engineering needs.

About the Role

We're looking for an Environmental Specialist to join our source testing team. You'll help measure and analyze emissions at industrial facilities such as power plants, paper mills, and chemical plants. You'll also do hands-on work in our lab. Recent graduates are welcome to apply. We'll train you in EPA stack testing methods and support you in earning your QSTI certification.

If you enjoy science and want a career that combines fieldwork, lab work, and travel instead of a desk job, this role is a good fit.

What You'll Do

Help conduct on-site emissions testing of industrial processes and pollution sources using EPA methods
Prepare, pack, and set up testing equipment and supplies before each project
Maintain, calibrate, and repair field testing equipment and lab instruments
Follow required test methods and standard operating procedures on every job
Record accurate, complete field data and lab results, including QA/QC documentation, for reports to clients and regulatory agencies
Prepare standard solutions and reagents for lab operations
Run routine chemical analyses using titrimetric, gravimetric, and volumetric procedures
Help maintain quality control and quality assurance records

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Engineering, or a related science field
Strong communication skills
Ability to analyze and interpret scientific data
Commitment to safety, accuracy, and ethical work
Experience in environmental or emissions testing is a plus
Knowledge of environmental regulations is a plus

Working Conditions

Overnight travel to client facilities, about 50% of the time, with trips usually lasting 2-3 days
Climbing ladders and working on elevated stack platforms
Working outdoors in heat, cold, and varying weather
Lifting and carrying equipment up to 50 lbs
Wearing required PPE, including respirators when needed
A valid driver's license and a clean driving record

What We Offer

Health, dental, and vision insurance
401(k)
Paid time off and holidays
Paid on-the-job training in EPA test methods
The stability of a company that has served industry for over 45 years

How to Apply

Send your resume to gretta@sandersengineering.com.

SEAS is an equal opportunity employer.

Our work brings together technical expertise and practical problem-solving to help clients move projects forward with clarity, quality, and confidence.

As part of our telecommunications environmental team, you will contribute to due diligence and regulatory review work that supports both property assessments and broader project delivery. Research property histories, review environmental records, conduct site reconnaissance and interviews, and evaluate potential environmental concerns
Develop clear conclusions regarding recognized environmental conditions, significant data gaps, and the need for additional investigation

Working effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams

jobs.title: Environmental Affairs Adviser (S)
jobs.description:
Background

This position is open for secondment only and participating States are kindly reminded that all costs in relation to an assignment at the Secretariat must be borne by their authorities.

The duties and requirements of this seconded (S) position correspond to a P3-level role in the UN common system. Candidates should, prior to applying, verify with their respective nominating authority to which extent financial remuneration and/or benefit packages will be offered. Seconded staff members in the OSCE Secretariat and Institutions are not entitled to a Board and Lodging Allowance payable by the Organization.

Note: This vacancy has been re-opened to expand the pool of nominations. Candidates who have already been nominated for this position remain under consideration and do not need to be renominated.

The OSCE has a comprehensive approach to security that encompasses politico-military, economic and environmental, and human aspects. It therefore addresses a wide range of security-related concerns, including arms control, confidence- and security-building measures, human rights, combating human trafficking, national minorities, democratization, policing strategies, counter-terrorism and economic and environmental activities. All 57 participating States enjoy equal status, and decisions are taken by consensus on a politically, but not legally binding basis.

The OSCE Secretariat in Vienna assists the Chairpersonship in its activities, and provides operational and administrative support to the field operations, and, as appropriate, to other institutions.

The Office of the Co-ordinator of OSCE Economic and Environmental Activities (OCEEA) deals with economic and environmental issues, operating under the premise that promoting economic prosperity and co-operation on environmental matters can contribute to international security and stability. The OCEEA helps the OSCE address economic, social and environmental aspects of security, through monitoring economic and environmental challenges among participating States and the implementation of OSCE commitments in that regard, strengthening co-operation between participating States in this area and collaboration with relevant international economic and environmental organizations, and developing tools, initiatives and dialogue platforms to facilitate economic and environmental co-operation and sustainable development.

Within this context, the OCEEA's Environmental Activities portfolio provides a platform for co-operation between participating States to address environmental issues, in relation to security objectives. It implements projects and activities related to sustainable use of natural resources, responses to impacts from climate change, energy security, and good environmental governance.

Tasks And Responsibilities

The main purpose of this position is to support OCEEA’s activities as well as the development, implementation and co-ordination of projects in the area of transboundary natural resource management and environmental governance, in close interaction with regional and local OSCE executive structures and other international actors, and to substantially contribute to policy advice and capacity-building workshops and events.

Working with minimum supervision, the Environmental Affairs Adviser provides expert advice on project implementation modalities and on the planning and conduct of programmatic activities in the field of environmental security, particularly transboundary water management, disaster risk reduction, climate resilience and good environmental governance. This includes guiding project design in line with OSCE standards, advising on partnerships and coordination mechanisms with OSCE structures and participating States, identifying priorities and opportunities for joint action, ensuring coherence with national and regional policies, and supporting effective delivery, reporting and visibility of programme activities.

The incumbent works under the direct supervision of the Senior Environmental Affairs Adviser while the Deputy Co-ordinator/Head, Environmental Activities acts as the second level supervisor.

More specifically, the Environmental Affairs Adviser performs the following tasks:

Developing, implementing and co-ordinating environmental projects in line with OSCE project management standards and in consultation with OSCE structures, delegations, field operations, experts and partners;
Identifying needs and priorities, ensuring alignment with national and regional policies, and adjusts project outputs to maximize OSCE added value and impact;
Organizing meetings, technical events, trainings and conferences, ensuring partner co-ordination, logistical arrangements and substantive contributions;
Establishing and maintaining target-oriented working relations with international and regional organizations, initiatives, business partners and NGOs to enhance synergies and monitor environmental trends;
Representing OCEEA at relevant meetings and events, analysing environmental developments, to inform participating States and OSCE structures;
Identifying opportunities for joint activities, supports co-ordinated programme development and sharing project results across partners and stakeholders;
Contributing to OCEEA policy and dialogue processes, including EEF, EEDIM and EEC, by preparing inputs, drafting speeches, statements, presentations and briefing materials;
Collecting and analysing environmental and social data and preparing reports, papers and other written outputs;
Promoting synergies with OCEEA's other programmes and liaising with the secretariat's other departments and OSCE structures to enhance impacts;
Mobilizing and maintaining funding for environmental activities, preparing concept notes, proposals and donor reports in coordination with relevant OSCE departments;
Enhancing visibility of OCEEA activities by preparing outreach materials and supporting events that communicate project results and engage funding partners.

Second-level university degree in Environmental Science, Economics, International Relations or Political Sciences, with a focus on environmental security issues. Recognized project management certification would be an asset;
A minimum of five years (seven years with a relevant first-level degree) of professional experience, preferably at the international/multilateral level;

Computer literate with practical experience in Microsoft applications.
