jobs.description:
Ramaker & Associates, Inc. is an employee-owned multidisciplinary firm delivering architecture, engineering, interior design, environmental, surveying, and related technical services for projects across a wide range of industries nationwide. Our work brings together technical expertise and practical problem-solving to help clients move projects forward with clarity, quality, and confidence.

As part of our telecommunications environmental team, you will contribute to due diligence and regulatory review work that supports both property assessments and broader project delivery. This role offers the opportunity to apply sound environmental judgment, collaborate across disciplines, and produce work that helps clients understand risk, navigate requirements, and make informed decisions.

Most of our projects are in the upper Midwest. We are looking for a candidate who will be within 1-2 hours driving distance from most of our project sites. When you are not at a job site, you have the flexibility to work from your home or from our office in Madison, Wisconsin.

Responsibilities

Prepare, review, and serve as the Environmental Professional for Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM E1527-21 and applicable All Appropriate Inquiries requirements
Research property histories, review environmental records, conduct site reconnaissance and interviews, and evaluate potential environmental concerns
Develop clear conclusions regarding recognized environmental conditions, significant data gaps, and the need for additional investigation
Support environmental and regulatory reviews for telecommunications projects, including NEPA documentation and permitting coordination, as appropriate to experience
Coordinate with engineers, surveyors, and multidisciplinary project teams to support environmental due diligence and project delivery
Analyze environmental data, maintain accurate project records, and assist with scopes of work, budgets, and technical report preparation

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Experience:
Preparing and reviewing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments under ASTM E1527-21 as an Environmental Professional
Researching property history, environmental records, and site investigation findings
Preparing technical reports, evaluating recognized environmental conditions, and supporting conclusions with sound professional judgment
Working effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams

Working knowledge of ASTM E1527-21, All Appropriate Inquiries requirements, and applicable environmental regulations
Eligibility to work in the United States without sponsorship
Willingness to travel to job sites approximately once per month, with occasional overnight stays

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Earth Science, Environmental Science and Management, Geology, or related field
Familiarity with NEPA documentation, permitting coordination, telecommunications project reviews, or the telecom market
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification

Benefits

Recognized as a Top Workplace by the Wisconsin State Journal five years in a row, Ramaker offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages and empowers employee-owners to pursue their professional goals in a collaborative and flexible work environment. This position is eligible for our full benefits package including health insurance with a company-funded health reimbursement account, dental, vision, life, disability, accident, critical illness, and pet insurance options. Additionally, we offer two retirement plans with our 401(k) plan with a company match and our employee stock ownership plan which is fully-funded by Ramaker. Ramaker supports your work/life balance by offering compressed workweeks, vacation, sick, and holiday pay.

Ramaker is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer that is committed to maintaining a welcoming, inclusive, and mutually respectful work environment for all. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or status as a protected veteran. If you need an accommodation as part of the employment process, please contact Human Resources at 608-643-4100 or at employment@ramaker.com.

jobs.description:
Title: Environmental Specialist II or Environmental Scientist II or Environmental Engineer II

Requisition ID: 146337

Location:

Safford, AZ, US, 85548

Category: Environmental

Share this Job

Why You Should Apply For This Job

At Freeport-McMoRan, we are committed to providing an employment package that recognizes excellence, encourages safe production and a culture supported by our core values. Here, you’ll find a collaborative environment where safety is a top priority, all opinions are valued, and people are empowered to grow in their career. Apply Today!   

Where You Will Work 

In operation since 2007, Safford operations is a zero-discharge facility and one of the most sustainable mines in the United States. The operation’s commitment to utilizing advanced technologies and sustainable practices strongly emphasizes safety and environmental stewardship. Located in southeastern Arizona, close to more than 4 million acres of national forest, employees and their families can connect with the great outdoors while fishing, rafting, hiking and more. Several educational institutions also are nearby, including a Northern Arizona University satellite campus, Eastern Arizona College, and the Gila Institute for Technology.  

Description

Under close supervision, assists in providing technical support and guidance for environmental projects and programs at assigned site.

Installs, operates, and maintains environmental and emission monitoring instruments and testing equipment. Analyzes data for compliance with regulatory requirements
Evaluates and assesses environmental risk and develops programs for risk reduction
Collaborates in recommending appropriate action to management in compliance with regulations
Reviews and/or Prepares and maintains detailed records and files of environmental data and communications
Evaluates and administers contracts with vendors for the provision of services and equipment
Maintains basic working knowledge of national, regional and local environmental, occupational health, and other applicable regulations. Maintains knowledge of site environmental policies and procedures
May provide leadership to less experienced engineers and technicians
May serve as Project Manager or technical expert on small to medium-sized environmental projects (e.g., compliance, remediation, or reclamation)
Leads or participates in regular audits and inspections of operations areas for purposes of ensuring compliance with site environmental policies, procedures and requirements of the Environmental Management System
Coordinates the timely recycling and disposition of materials and other company assets in compliance with applicable legal and other requirements
Tracks and reports the recycling and disposition of materials and other company assets as directed
Performs other duties as assigned

Qualifications

What You Bring To Freeport

Associate's Degree in Environmental Science or closely related area (can substitute an additional five (5) years of experience in mining or mineral processing operations for the degree requirement) and
Seven (7) years' experience in environmental monitoring, sampling and reporting as an Environmental Technician , Specialist or in a closely related role
Additional certification or licensure appropriate to the job may be required or preferred: (US Examples include: HAZWOPER, Method 9, DOT, EMS Auditor, Asbestos, Water Treatment Operator, or CHMM.)

OR

Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Environmental, Civil, Chemical, Agricultural, Mining, Metallurgical, Geological or similar) and at least three (3) years environmental or related experience; OR
Master’s degree in Engineering in a related field and at least one (1) year environmental or related experience.
Additional certification or licensure appropriate to the job may be required or preferred such as HAZWOPER, Method 9, DOT, EMS Auditor, Asbestos, Water Treatment Operator, or CHMM.

OR

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Technology, Earth Science or related natural science (such as Biology, Chemistry, Geology, Hydrology, Forestry, Agriculture, Meteorology, Environmental/Natural Resource Management) or Mathematics/Computer Science including Accounting and Finance, or Business Management or other Bachelor’s degree, and at least three (3) years environmental or related experience; OR
Master’s degree in a related field and at least one (1) year environmental or related experience.
Additional certification or licensure appropriate to the job may be required or preferred including HAZWOPER, Method 9, DOT, EMS Auditor, Asbestos, Water Treatment Operator, or CHMM.

Preferred

Knowledge in Water Quality including APP, SWPPP, SPCC. Project Management experience. Grade 2 Domestic Water Operator Certified in both Distribution and Treatment. Experience with working with Operations and Maintenance personnel in Industrial setting. Proficient in Enablon, EQuIS, and Microsoft Office tools.

Criteria/Conditions

Ability to understand and apply verbal and written work and safety-related instructions and procedures given in English
Ability to communicate in English with respect to job assignments, job procedures, and applicable safety standards
Work is in a mine or manufacturing plant setting, which may include exposure to extremes in temperature and humidity, moving mechanical parts, risk of electrical shock, toxic chemicals, explosives, fumes or airborne particles
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, sit, demonstrate manual dexterity, climb stairs and ladders, work on elevated platforms, talk, hear and see
Occasionally may be required to lift moderately heavy objects (up to 30 pounds) during the course of the workday
Personal protective equipment is required when performing work in a mine, outdoor, manufacturing or plant environment, including hard hat, hearing protection, safety glasses, safety footwear, and as needed, respirator, rubber steel-toe boots, protective clothing, gloves and any other protective equipment as required
Freeport-McMoRan promotes a drug/alcohol free work environment through the use of mandatory pre-employment drug testing and on-going random drug testing

What We Offer You 

The estimated annual pay range for this role is currently  $87,500-$120,000.
 This range reflects base salary only and does not include bonus payments, benefits or retirement contributions. Actual base pay is determined by experience, qualifications, skills and other job-related factors. This role is eligible for additional discretionary and incentive payment considerations based on company and individual performance. More details will be shared during the hiring process. Click here to view a sample of Total Rewards Estimate for this role.  

Affordable medical, dental and vision benefits  
Company-paid life and disability insurance  
401(k) plan with employer contribution/match  
Paid time off, paid sick time, holiday pay, parental leave  
Tuition assistance  
Employee Assistance Program  
Discounted insurance plans for pet, auto, home and vehicle  
Internal progression opportunities  
Learn more about our competitive and comprehensive benefits package! 

   What We Require 

Candidates may be required to pass a medical exam.  
Candidates must pass all required training and/or testing.  
Employees may be required to work a non-standard schedule, which may include shift work (other than day shift) at a 24/7, 365-day operation.  
Freeport-McMoRan promotes a drug/alcohol-free work environment using mandatory pre-employment drug testing and on-going drug and alcohol testing, as allowed by applicable laws. 

Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description:
Position Overview

This position provides project management and technical leadership of environmental investigation and remediation projects, as well as assists in the development of technical staff to meet client and organizational needs.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in relevant technical field.
Minimum of 7 years of environmental consulting experience.
Holds professional certification as a P.E., or absent certification, a minimum of 7 years working with a licensed professional.
Proficient in performing senior level interpretation work including remedial cost estimates, future remedial measures selection, and costing.
Experience performing conceptual and detailed remedial design work.
Demonstrated project management skills.
Advanced data evaluation and analytical skills.
Proficient written and verbal communication skills.
Experience interacting with clients and regulatory agencies.
Ability and willingness to support the technical growth of project/staff level professionals based on direct hands-on interactions.

Essential Duties

Project Management:
Manage projects including key responsibilities for scheduling and coordination of project resources to meet client and organizational needs.
Ensure that individual task schedules, budgets, and client invoicing are performed in accordance with Company standards and client requirements to complete project work.

Technical Data Review and Report Preparation:
Coordinate and provide quality control for data collection and review of project results, including the reduction of field data to evaluate and determine future client needs and project requirements.
Interpret data, develop, and finalize a report for Project Principal’s review that appropriately documents findings and project remediation recommendations.

Proposal Preparation and Business Development:
Assist with the preparation of proposals, cost estimates, and with marketing activities.

Staff Mentoring and Training:
Participate in the development of junior staff and work with senior management to continue to grow as a consultant and leader of the firm.

Physical Demands/Work Environment Conditions

This position occasionally works in the field, and predominantly works in an office environment. In the field, candidate will be working independently or more commonly will be leading a larger team at exterior project sites (i.e., industrial/brownfield facilities, monitoring wells, treatment systems, construction projects) to perform sample collection, recording of operational/meter parameters, and oversight of subcontractors (e.g., drillers, heavy equipment operators, truckers). These field activities require the ability to drive to different project sites and physically move around outdoors in various terrains, and occasionally in adverse weather conditions. Office work is primarily stationary/sedentary using a computer and keyboard/mouse requiring repetitive hand movements.

Actual compensation may vary based on job-related factors such as relevant work experience , market conditions, education /training, certifications, skill sets, and internal equity. Job Summary

The Restoration Technician is responsible for working as part of a team to perform emergency services and contents restoration work while adhering to company policies and procedures regarding remediation. The individual will also adhere to EPA, OSHA, and local requirements regarding safety and hazardous materials handling. Other qualifications and responsibilities might arise as deemed necessary by circumstances. The individual must be available for emergency response work after-hours and on weekends.

Responsibilities

Perform content restoration work residential and commercial properties
Perform physical labor associated with cleanup activities, packing customers' contents, general on-location cleaning, HVAC cleaning and deodorization of facilities
Assists with the inventory of site contents, setup of emergency services equipment, preparing contents for storage and lifting items into storage
Follow applicable safety rules, regulations, guidelines, policies and site specific safety plans when performing cleanup activities and donning protective gear
Operate routinely used tools and equipment
Perform routine inspection and preventative maintenance on assigned equipment
Warehouse maintenance, stock supplies, building maintenance
Perform work at high elevations such as from a ladder and scaffolding
Hazardous Waste Operations
All other duties as assigned

Technical Skills:
Ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ration and percent.

Communication Skills --
Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions and procedure manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers or employees of organization.

Work Environment:
Working around equipment and machinery, the work environment is usually dirty, dusty and noisy, on uneven ground/surfaces containing hazardous or potentially hazardous substances and/or materials and is subject to inclement or extreme weather conditions and temperatures. Work includes handling hazardous materials and use of personal protective equipment. Frequent travel is required for this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Physical Demands
: Must be in good physical health and be able to meet the medical clearance requirements of an OSHA (HAZWOPER) medical surveillance physical examination and drug screening. Able to wear full and half face respirator, work in confined spaces and regularly lift and carry 75 pounds.

2-4 years of Construction experience, working on water/fire damage jobs specifically, environmental experience and hazardous waste.

Certifications Needed:
The individual must have on file a valid and current environmental physical enabling the individual to wear a respirator. Also, OSHA 40 hr. HAZWOPER, current State Driver's license and forklift operator certification.

Additional Eligibility Qualifications:
Construction industry experience preferred. IICRC Water Restoration certification is a plus. Heavy equipment operation and maintenance experience a plus. The successful candidate will have a positive attitude, strong work ethic with the ability to follow directions. Good communication skills and commitment to company safety policy are a must. Must be legally eligible to work in the United States. Bilingual English/Spanish is encouraged, but not required.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist, Senior
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Senior Director of Environmental, you will serve as the Sr. Environmental Specialist responsible for optimizing the daily performance of wastewater treatment systems across Conagra's manufacturing network. You will lead initiatives to improve reliability and efficiency of lagoon treatment, dissolved air flotation, neutralization, and equalization systems while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations. You will provide technical guidance, analyze system data, and support operator training to maintain best-in-class wastewater operations.

This position can be based in: Fayetteville AR, Russellville AR, Fort Madison IA Imlay City, MI, Archbold OH, Council Bluffs IA, Marshall MO, Troy OH or Darien WI

A Taste of Your Responsibilities

Serve as the subject matter expert on wastewater treatment process design, control, and troubleshooting.
Collaborate with engineering, maintenance, and environmental health and safety teams to evaluate system modifications and upgrades.
Lead process monitoring and optimization of lagoon treatment, dissolved air flotation, equalization, and neutralization systems.
Evaluate biological and chemical treatment performance through sampling, laboratory analysis, and data trending.
Develop operational playbooks and standardized procedures across the manufacturing network.
Travel to multiple sites to identify and implement process improvements that optimize treatment efficiency, energy use, and chemical consumption.
Support daily operation of pumps, aerators, clarifiers, and other treatment infrastructure.
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local wastewater discharge permits and environmental regulations.
Establish standards for operational logs, sampling records, and performance reporting.
Support preparation of permit applications, renewals, and regulatory inspections.
Develop and deliver training for operators and plant personnel on treatment system operation, safety, and best practices.

Ingredients Required for Your Success

Bachelor’s degree in environmental engineering, chemical engineering, civil engineering, environmental science, or related field.
5+ years of experience in operation and optimization of industrial or municipal wastewater treatment systems.
Experience with lagoon treatment systems, dissolved air flotation units, neutralization, and equalization processes.
Experience interpreting operational data, identifying trends, and implementing corrective actions.
Experience with supervisory control and data acquisition systems, laboratory testing, and process control strategies.
Strong communication skills to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Experience with wastewater solids management and agricultural land application preferred.
Wastewater operator certification or Engineer in Training or Professional Engineer designation preferred.
Willing to travel 50%

Physical Requirements

Requirements

More information about essential tasks and the facility will be shared during the hiring process. This role may require you to be in our manufacturing facilities. When visiting these sites, the physical requirements below may apply:

You may be required to walk around the facility, climb stairs/ladders, kneel, or perform repetitive tasks that require hand-eye coordination.

You may be required to lift or carry materials that can vary in weight and size.

This is a manufacturing environment with large, moving equipment. Noise levels can be high, and temperatures may vary.

Compensation

Pay Range:$82,000-$120,000

The annual salary listed above is the expected offering for this position. An employee’s actual annual salary will be based on but not limited to: location, relevant experience/level and skillset, while balancing internal Conagra employees’ equity. Conagra Brands will comply with applicable law regarding minimum salaries for exempt employees.

Our Benefits

We care about your total well-being and will support you with the following, subject to your location and role:

Health: Comprehensive healthcare plans, wellness incentive program, mental wellbeing support and fitness reimbursement
Wealth: Great pay, bonus incentive opportunity, matching 401(k) and stock purchase plan
Growth: Career development opportunities, employee resource groups, on-demand learning and tuition reimbursement
Balance: Paid-time off, parental leave, flexible work-schedules (subject to your location and role) and volunteer opportunities

Our Company

At Conagra Brands, we have a rich heritage of making great food. We aspire to have the most impactful, energized and inclusive culture in food. As a member of our 18,000+ person team across 40+ locations, you are empowered to reach your potential, make an impact and own your career. We're in the business of building champions – within our people and our iconic brands like Birds Eye®, Slim Jim® and Reddi-Wip®.

Our focus on innovation extends beyond making great food, it also reflects our commitment to embracing new solutions that positively impact our team, the communities we serve and the health of our planet. Foodies Welcome.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Title: Environmental Advisor

Location: Plymouth (with travel to surrounding areas)

About Us

Galliford Try is one of the UK’s most formidable construction businesses with an enviable track record of delivering schemes that strive to provide positive, lasting change for the communities we work in. As a FTSE 250 organisation, we turnover £1.5 billion and employ over 3,500 people across four successful Divisions: Building, Infrastructure, Environment and Specialist Services.

As one of the UK’s leading principal contractors, you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the country’s most exciting projects, offering long-term stability alongside the chance to stretch your capabilities and realise your career goals. You will be joining diverse, high-performing teams with exceptional levels of commitment.

Our Environment Division

Our Environment Division provides source to sea asset delivery capability across the UK and Scotland, working on both framework and standalone projects. Since AMP3, we have delivered more than £2bn of assets for clients including Yorkshire Water, United Utilities, Anglian Water, Thames Water, Southern Water, Welsh Water and Scottish Water.

This is an exciting time to join the business as we continue to evolve and prepare for delivery in a future digital world.

As Environmental Advisor

jobs.description:
Job Description

You can play an important part in disaster relief missions as a Geospatial Engineer for the Army National Guard. In this role, you will extract and supply geographic data that supports military operations of all kinds and help commanders visualize the battlefield during combat.

As a Geospatial Engineer, your primary responsibility will be to collect and process military geographic information from decentralized sources (remote sensed imagery, digital data, intelligence data, existing topographic products, and other collateral data sources), present this information to leaders, and return decisions to the field.

You May Also

Supervise topographic surveying, cartography, and photolithography activities
Assist in topographic planning and control activities
Assist in determining requirements and providing technical supervision of geographic intelligence programs

Job Duties

Create geographic data and compile them into maps
Create and maintain multiple geospatial databases
Prepare military-style briefs covering all aspects of the terrain

Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn

Basic knowledge of Geographic Information Systems
Imagery interpretation and exploitation

Helpful Skills

Interest in geography, maps, and charts
Ability to demonstrate basic computer skills and work with drafting equipment
Conceptualize ideas into computer-generated 2-D/3-D geospatial products
Preference for a technical career field

Through your training, you will develop the skills and experience to enjoy a civilian career with construction, engineering, and architectural firms, as well as with government agencies as a surveyor, mapmaker, cartographer, cartographic technician, or photogrammetrist.

Earn While You Learn

Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to train. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance.

Job training for a Geospatial Engineer requires 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you'll learn basic Soldiering skills, and 20 weeks of Advanced Individual Training (AIT) and on-the-job instruction, including practical application of geographic information systems. Part of this time is spent in the classroom and part in the field.

Benefits/Requirements

Benefits

Paid training
A monthly paycheck
Montgomery GI Bill
Federal and State tuition assistance
Retirement benefits for part-time service
Low-cost life insurance (up to $400,000 in coverage)
401(k)-type savings plan
Student Loan Repayment Program (up to $50,000, for existing loans)
Health care benefits available
VA home loans
Bonuses, if applicable
Most non-prior service candidates will earn between $200 and $250 per drill weekend, subject to change

Military enlistment in the Army National Guard
Must be at least a junior in high school, or have a high school diploma or a GED certificate
Must be between the ages of 17 and 35
Must be able to pass a physical exam and meet legal and moral standards
Must meet citizenship requirements (see NATIONALGUARD.com for details)

Requires military enlistment. Programs and benefits are subject to change. Ask your Army National Guard recruiter for the most up-to-date information. Actual MOS assignment may depend on MOS availability.

jobs.title: Senior GIS Developer
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior GIS Developer based in United States.

The Senior GIS Developer will build and support GIS solutions that enable complex business and network operations.

The role combines advanced GIS expertise with strong software-development and automation capabilities.

You will work across QGIS, ArcGIS, enterprise databases, web technologies, and spatial data systems.

Your work will support mapping, network analysis, data management, and operational workflows at scale.

You will also contribute to GIS architecture, standards, system integrations, and innovative tooling.

The position offers an opportunity to collaborate within an Agile/Scrum environment on highly impactful geospatial solutions.

Strong technical judgment, analytical thinking, and attention to data quality will be essential to success.

Accountabilities

Design, develop, and support server-based geoprocessing tools and automated data-update processes using Python and SQL, helping streamline recurring GIS operations and improve data reliability.
Build, deploy, maintain, and enhance custom QGIS plugins and forms using Python, PyQGIS, and Qt-based interfaces to support data acquisition, editing, validation, geoprocessing, and integration with other systems.
Partner with GIS engineering leadership to advance custom GIS tools, system integrations, and solution architecture, while contributing to architecture diagrams and technical design decisions.
Design and implement organization-wide GIS standards across server, cloud, web, desktop, and enterprise database environments to promote consistency, scalability, and maintainability.
Build and maintain FME Flow or Python-based ETL and scheduled data-processing workflows that automate mapping, data management, and recurring GIS activities.
Develop and maintain network-routing solutions using shortest-path algorithms while accounting for complex dependencies, constraints, spatial relationships, and business requirements.
Produce technical documentation, coding standards, workflow guidance, and training materials, while supporting knowledge transfer through demonstrations and remote training sessions.
Contribute throughout the software-development lifecycle within an Agile/Scrum team, collaborating with technical and business stakeholders to deliver reliable GIS capabilities.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Computer Science, or a closely related discipline, supported by a strong understanding of geographic concepts and principles, along with 5–7 years of relevant GIS and software-development experience.
Advanced Python skills applied to GIS automation, geoprocessing, ArcGIS web applications, REST services, and network-analysis workflows, with strong SQL and relational database experience, preferably including PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
Strong knowledge of Esri ArcGIS technologies, including desktop, online, server, enterprise databases, vector data, geoprocessing, and spatial-analysis capabilities, combined with hands-on QGIS and PyQGIS experience.
Practical experience creating QGIS plugins, custom processing tools, forms, or workflow extensions, as well as experience with FME-based or Python-driven ETL and automated processing workflows.
Strong web-development capabilities using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with experience working with ArcGIS JavaScript APIs, Web AppBuilder, ArcGIS Server services, REST APIs, and other integration technologies.
Solid understanding of software-development lifecycle practices, source control, testing, debugging, maintainable code design, algorithms, data structures, data modeling, and distributed systems, particularly as applied to spatial and network problems.
Strong knowledge of vector data, geoprocessing, spatial analysis, coordinate systems, topology, and network-routing concepts, supported by excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.
Experience designing or consuming APIs and integrating GIS platforms with external business or operational systems, with strong attention to accuracy, data quality, and technical detail.
Experience in telecommunications, outside plant (OSP), fiber network inventory, route planning, network design, or other comparable network-oriented environments is highly valuable.
Demonstrated ability to lead user training, develop technical process documentation, support GIS users across multiple teams, and communicate complex technical concepts effectively.

Benefits

Estimated annual base salary of $95,100–$146,300 USD, with actual compensation determined by factors such as geographic location, experience, skills, certifications, and organizational needs.
Potential eligibility for a discretionary annual incentive plan for non-sales roles.
Excellent health, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement savings through a 401(k) plan.
Generous paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Remote work opportunity within the United States.
Opportunity to work on large-scale GIS, network, spatial-data, automation, and systems-integration initiatives.
The position does not provide employment-based visa sponsorship or assume responsibility for employment visa or work authorization sponsorship now or in the future.

Excellent organization skills and attention to detail.

Experience in Database, Esri suite of software, AutoCAD 2d, AutoCAD Civil 3d and/or MicroStation.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist I
jobs.description:
Aqua, an Essential Utilities company, employs people in a variety of roles within our eight-state footprint, ranging from field workers and customer service representatives who are on the front lines working with customers, to scientists and engineers who help ensure we’re delivering reliable water and wastewater services to our communities. If you’re looking for a rewarding career helping improve our environment and protect our natural resources, we encourage you to join our team!

About Essential Utilities

Essential Utilities, Inc. delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities.

Operating as the Aqua (water and wastewater services) and the Peoples and Delta (natural gas) brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across 10 states. We are committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status - including a competitive and comprehensive benefits package as well as a commitment to career growth opportunities.

We are advocates for the communities we serve and are dedicated stewards of natural lands, protecting more than 7,600 acres of forests and other habitats throughout our footprint.

Our company is one of the most significant publicly traded water, wastewater service and natural gas providers in the U.S.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Conducts leak detection investigations and system surveys of Aqua‑owned water and wastewater facilities, distribution mains, service lines, hydrants, valves, and related infrastructure to identify real water losses, unaccounted‑for water, and potential infrastructure failures.
Performs or supports acoustic, pressure, flow, and meter data analysis to assist with leak location, verification, and prioritization of repairs.
Coordinates with Operations, Engineering, and outside contractors during leak detection surveys, field investigations, and corrective actions.
Documents findings from leak detection activities, prepares summary reports, and enters results into tracking systems or databases to support asset management and regulatory reporting.
Assists with investigation and response to customer complaints related to suspected leaks, pressure concerns, or unexplained water usage.
Supports water loss control initiatives by collecting field data used for water audits, system evaluations, and infrastructure improvement planning.
Issues work orders or repair recommendations based on identified leaks or system deficiencies and tracks corrective actions to completion.
Participates in field work associated with emergency response, system failures, or regulatory inquiries related to water loss or distribution system integrity.
Schedules sampling for all systems at the appropriate times and assists operators and managers with sampling issues. Records and monitors test results on Excel or database spreadsheets. Contacts the state to correct any discrepancies. Ensures compliance with sampling requirements by reviewing chain of custody forms, checks sample codes, and works with the labs to ensure complete and accurate paperwork for each sample and track sample results. Ensures that all monthly and quarterly samples are collected. Reviews the test results for compliance. Reports any exceeding amounts to the responsible departments (internal managers).
Drafts compliance reports and compiles data for reports. Organizes and tracks compliance work for inclusion in reports, including field data. Issues work orders and schedules for additional compliance work. Plots and graphs data, and tracks compliance. Ensures timely preparation and filing of all compliance reports and permits.
Reviews inspection reports and regulatory correspondence. Shares information with others electronically and drafts response letters. Issues work orders for compliance repairs. Meets with operators and managers to discuss inspection reports. Works with engineer and managers to draft responses.
Coordinates, drafts, and issues any public notices as required working with management, engineering, and staff.
Assists in the resolution or response to compliance.
Prepares and maintains sampling plans including monthly bacteriological, lead and copper, disinfection by-products, and others for all systems and updates sample sites as needed. Ensures all samples are collected and reviews data.
Answers customer inquiries regarding analysis results and distributing copies of results if needed. Provides administrative support to Engineering Department. Processes invoices, copy, route and file documents as needed.
Prepares reports and tracks progress of budgeted project work.
Participates in meetings and other activities of Aqua as required.
Collects data from flow recorder data recorders and pressure recorders. Downloads data to PC and plot data.
Assists in the development of operating and capital budgets. Assists with permit reviews, renewals, and special or new monitoring requirements.
Provides input and assistance with preliminary design, project management, and contractor coordination for compliance-related capital projects, as needed.
Communicate urgent information to supervisors and operators and customers regarding water quality inquiries. Serve in an advisory/training capacity towards plant staff on sampling and proper test procedures to ensure compliance.
Performs other assignments as required.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Activities, duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

Education Requirements

Associate Degree; Bachelor’s degree preferred

Specialized Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of water distribution systems, leak detection principles, and water loss control concepts preferred.
Ability to interpret flow, pressure, and acoustic data from field monitoring equipment.
Ability to perform field investigations under varying weather and site conditions.

Professional Certification and Licenses

Ohio EPA Water Distribution II license or the ability to obtain the license within 2 years of employment.

Experience Level

1–2 years of related experience (environmental compliance, water distribution, leak detection, or utility field work preferred).

Office Technology Level

Competent to use Microsoft Office suite: Word‚ PowerPoint and Excel.

Communication Skills

Uses skills needed to obtain or provide routine information and answer some routine and technical questions; Communication often requires some interpretation (e.g. dealing with inquiries).

Driver’s License Required

Yes

Overall Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and arms.

Field work may require extended walking, standing, and working in uneven terrain, roadway environments, vaults, or excavation areas while performing leak detection surveys and investigations.

Equal employment opportunity is provided to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to the following legally protected characteristics: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, pregnancy (including childbirth and related medical conditions, including medical conditions related to lactation), physical or mental disability, covered-veteran status, genetic information (including testing and characteristics), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression or any other characteristic protected by applicable local, state or federal law.

Aqua is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you have a condition that may prevent you from applying for a job online or need to request an accommodation during the interview process, please call (1-877-271-9012).

Family members cannot result in a supervisor/subordinate reporting relationship
Family members cannot work in the same department.

jobs.title: 12Y Geospatial Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description

You can play an important part in disaster relief missions as a Geospatial Engineer for the Army National Guard. In this role, you will extract and supply geographic data that supports military operations of all kinds and help commanders visualize the battlefield during combat.

As a Geospatial Engineer, your primary responsibility will be to collect and process military geographic information from decentralized sources (remote sensed imagery, digital data, intelligence data, existing topographic products, and other collateral data sources), present this information to leaders, and return decisions to the field.

You May Also

Supervise topographic surveying, cartography, and photolithography activities
Assist in topographic planning and control activities
Assist in determining requirements and providing technical supervision of geographic intelligence programs

Job Duties

Create geographic data and compile them into maps
Create and maintain multiple geospatial databases
Prepare military-style briefs covering all aspects of the terrain

Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn

Basic knowledge of Geographic Information Systems
Imagery interpretation and exploitation

Helpful Skills

Interest in geography, maps, and charts
Ability to demonstrate basic computer skills and work with drafting equipment
Conceptualize ideas into computer-generated 2-D/3-D geospatial products
Preference for a technical career field

Through your training, you will develop the skills and experience to enjoy a civilian career with construction, engineering, and architectural firms, as well as with government agencies as a surveyor, mapmaker, cartographer, cartographic technician, or photogrammetrist.

Earn While You Learn

Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to train. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance.

Job training for a Geospatial Engineer requires 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you'll learn basic Soldiering skills, and 20 weeks of Advanced Individual Training (AIT) and on-the-job instruction, including practical application of geographic information systems. Part of this time is spent in the classroom and part in the field.

jobs.title: Senior BIM Engineer - Geo Environmental Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

The suitable candidate for this role is a Senior BIM Engineer specialising in Geo-Environmental, Civil infrastructure projects, with a strong focus on digital delivery and Civil 3D modelling. The role involves close coordination with design engineers and multidisciplinary teams across India and global regions, supporting project delivery through high-quality CAD and 3D modelling outputs.

The Senior BIM Engineer will take ownership of 3D modelling, drafting, and preparation of design documentation for Geo-Environmental, civil infrastructure, including water supply, wastewater, stormwater systems, and utility networks. The role supports projects across all stages, from concept and preliminary design through to detailed design and construction documentation.

Key responsibilities include developing and maintaining Civil 3D models (surfaces, alignments, corridors, pipe networks), integrating GIS and survey data, ensuring QA/QC compliance, and delivering accurate, coordinated, and construction-ready digital deliverables aligned with project standards and client expectations.

Responsibilities

RESPONSIBILITIES

Develop, review, and maintain high-quality 2D and 3D CAD models and drawings for Geo-Environmental, civil infrastructure projects, ensuring accuracy and compliance with project requirements, Australian standards, and company guidelines.
Produce and manage detailed 3D civil models in Autodesk Civil 3D, including surfaces, alignments, profiles, corridors, grading, and utility models.
Prepare accurate engineering drawings and documentation, including plans, sections, long sections, details, and construction drawings suitable for tender and construction stages.
Manage and process spatial/geospatial data (GIS/CAD) to support design development, analysis, and project documentation workflows.
Coordinate closely with engineers, designers, and multidisciplinary teams to ensure design intent, technical standards, and project requirements are fully achieved.
Lead the coordination and integration of digital design models across disciplines (civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical) to ensure clash-free and constructible solutions.
Maintain and enforce CAD/BIM standards, naming conventions, and modelling best practices, ensuring consistency and quality across deliverables.
Perform quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) checks and audits of drawings and models in line with project specifications, company standards, and client requirements.
Support data exchange and interoperability workflows, including GIS/CAD integration, model sharing, and preparation of digital deliverables for clients and contractors.
Collaborate with project stakeholders (engineers, architects, project managers, and external partners) to resolve design issues, improve efficiency, and optimise design solutions.
Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and support to junior modellers and drafters, promoting knowledge sharing and capability development within the team.
Develop and maintain CAD libraries, templates, and standard details to enhance productivity, consistency, and efficiency across projects.
Participate in design reviews and project meetings, contributing technical input on modelling strategies, constructability, and digital delivery approaches.
Manage multiple project deliverables simultaneously, prioritising tasks effectively to meet deadlines while maintaining a high standard of quality.
Stay up to date with latest CAD/BIM technologies, industry trends, and digital engineering practices, proactively recommending improvements and innovation opportunities.
Support implementation of BIM and digital engineering workflows, including model coordination, federated models, and alignment with ISO/BIM standards where applicable.
Ensure document control, version management, and deliverable compliance throughout the project lifecycle.

Required Technical And Soft Skills

Advanced proficiency in Autodesk Civil 3D, including development of detailed civil infrastructure models and drawings:
Creation and management of corridors, alignments, profiles, and assemblies for road, drainage, and utility designs
Development of surface models, grading solutions, and earthworks design
Modelling of pipe networks (stormwater, water, wastewater) with annotations, schedules, and documentation
Preparation of drawing sheets, plan production workflows, and construction documentation
Effective use of data shortcuts and reference management for large, multidisciplinary project environments
Ensuring model integrity, coordination across disciplines, and adherence to standards and deliverables

GIS and Spatial Data Integration (Basic to Intermediate):
Working knowledge of spatial data formats (SHP, DEM, raster datasets)
Understanding of coordinate systems, projections, and georeferencing
Integration of GIS data into Civil 3D workflows for terrain modelling and design analysis
Interpretation of topographical, cadastral, and environmental datasets
Awareness of data quality, accuracy, and transformation processes
Support for CAD–GIS integration workflows to enhance design and digital deliverables

Survey, Point Cloud, and Data Processing:
Experience in survey data processing, including raw data handling, field codes, and survey database management
Exposure to point cloud processing (LiDAR/laser scans) and integration into design models

Digital Engineering, BIM, and Information Management:
Familiarity with Common Data Environments (CDEs) such as Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), ProjectWise, or similar
Understanding of ISO 19650 standards and digital information management principles
Awareness of data governance, security, and information management practices
Exposure to 4D/5D BIM concepts (construction sequencing, quantities, cost integration – desirable)

Automation, Interoperability, and Advanced Tools:
Experience with design automation and customisation (Dynamo for Civil 3D, basic AutoLISP/Python – advantageous)
Familiarity with interoperability standards and file formats (IFC, LandXML, SHP, DWG workflows)
Capability in model-based quantity take-offs and estimation support

Quality, Coordination, and Collaboration:
Strong capability in data validation, model health checks, and automated QA/QC processes
Experience working in cloud-based collaboration environments and remote coordination workflows
Proven ability to work in multidisciplinary and cross-regional project teams

Professional & Leadership Skills
Strong communication, coordination, and stakeholder engagement skills
Demonstrated technical leadership and mentoring capability
High attention to quality, accuracy, and detail, with ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
Proactive, self-driven, and solution-oriented mindset, with adaptability to new technologies
Commitment to Health & Safety, sustainability, and WSP Future Ready® principles

Software Proficiencies

Demonstrated advanced hands-on expertise in AutoCAD Civil 3D & BIM coordination is a critical requirement for this role.
Extensive hands-on experience in AutoCAD (2D), Navisworks are essential with additional exposure to ArchGIS, QGIS, Revit, 12D, OpenRoads considered an advantage.

Proven experience in using Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) and BIM 360 platforms for project delivery and collaboration. Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

Qualifications

Qualification of a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, or (B.Tech or equivalent) in a relevant engineering discipline

Experience

8–16 years of proven experience in water supply and wastewater utility projects.
Hands-on experience in Civil 3D modelling and GIS integration, with the ability to develop accurate, coordinated models and effectively utilise spatial data to support civil infrastructure design and documentation.
Proven experience in AU/ NZ projects is highly preferred, with additional exposure to UK, US, or Middle East projects considered an advantage.

jobs.title: Technical Director- Environmental Planning
jobs.description:
Job Description

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Who are we looking for?

GHD is looking for a Technical Director - Environmental Planning
in any of the following California offices: San Diego, Irvine, Los Angeles, Long Beach, San Francisco, Oakland, Concord, Sacramento, or Santa Rosa
. The ideal candidate must be recognized as an industry leader and have significant experience in business development, contributing to growth of practice areas, overseeing the environmental review process, and winning and leading projects of importance.

Our Natural Resources & Impact Assessment Group provides environmental impact documentation and permitting services for a broad range of interesting clients and projects, working across multiple geographies throughout California and the Pacific. Our work extends across a diverse range of market sectors, including transportation (ports, road, rail, and transit), utilities, local development, energy, mining, and coastal restoration.

Our Hybrid Work Model: B
e part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Responsibilities

Business Development and Growth: Lead all phases of winning work including positioning, pipeline development, pursuits, developing new clients, and maintaining client relationships to increase opportunity pipeline and bookings.
Project Delivery: Manage multi-disciplinary teams and preparation of CEQA/NEPA environmental documents, environmental technical studies, and regulatory permitting, including for large or complex projects in a client-facing setting.
Technical Leadership: Provide internal and external leadership to provide senior technical leadership and increase industry standing. Maintain external accreditations and in-depth understanding of current and emerging technologies, external regulation, and industry best practices through continuing professional development, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Mentoring and Recruitment: Support recruitment activities and growth of new environmental service areas. Foster teamwork and actively support the ongoing development and retention of staff.
Organizational Capability Building: Evaluate the capabilities of staff within the department to identify gaps and prioritize development activities. Implement the organization's formal development frameworks within the area of responsibility. Coach and mentor others to support the development of the organization's talent pool.
Policy Development and Implementation: Develop functional or operational policies and help develop policy frameworks for area of responsibility or department. Take responsibility for creating underlying procedures and monitoring their implementation.
Functional Strategy Formation: Lead the development and implementation of strategy for a significant area of responsibility, anticipating complex issues, challenges, and opportunities and ensuring integration with wider corporate strategy.
Project Management: Manage a portfolio of major projects in line with overall project management strategy.
Community of Practice Management: Contribute strongly on a strategically significant area to a community of practice in a defined area of expertise or consulting, or lead on an area of expertise or consulting practice, to contribute to thought leadership and to develop innovative practice among colleagues.
Health, Safety, and Environment: Ensure that business activities and individuals (e.g., employees, contractors, and visitors) within the area of responsibility adhere to the organization's health, safety, and environment (HSE) policies, procedures, and mandatory instructions, to safeguard the environment, protect the well-being of individuals, and minimize business risk.
Client & Customer Management (External): Manage key client and customer relationships. Likely to involve using account teams to maintain customer satisfaction and loyalty.

Education

Bachelor’s and/or Master's Degree in environmental studies, environmental science, planning, geography, public administration, or a related field

Experience

Minimum of 20+ years of experience providing most or all essential responsibilities noted above.
Comprehensive knowledge of the CEQA, NEPA, and applicable state and federal regulations and significant project experience in the preparation of environmental documentation, permitting, mitigation planning and implementation, and environmental compliance.
Significant experience with all phases of winning work including positioning, pipeline development, pursuits, developing new clients, and maintaining client relationships.
Excellent analytical, organizational, time management, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills.
Commitment to delivering and producing quality work within established budgets and schedules.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Bring your curiosity and determination to make a positive impact on the future of mining!
Together and with our mining clients, we will create a lasting community benefit making water, energy, and communities sustainable for generations to come.

Be a project manager delivering services to our mining clients.
Work on exciting mining projects for new and existing clients. Showcase your technical capabilities and expertise.

Join GHD.

Who are we looking for?

GHD’s U.S West Mining Team is seeking a motivated Project Manager
to join our Mining Team and support the planning, execution, and delivery of legacy mine reclamation and remediation projects. This role is ideal for a technically skilled professional with approximately five years of industry experience who is ready to transition into project management. Working under the guidance of senior project managers, the successful candidate will coordinate project activities, support client communications, manage schedules and budgets, and help deliver projects safely, on time, and within budget.

Join an employee-owned firm that will invest in your growth and development. GHD is the place for aspiring people like you to thrive, achieve your career goals, and make a lasting impact.

This position can be based in any of our offices across the West region ( Phoenix, AZ; Tucson, AZ; Sacramento, CA; Roseville, CA; Seattle, WA; Irvine, CA; Eureka, CA; Concord, CA; Bay Area, CA, Redding, CA).

Our Hybrid Work Model
: Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Initiate and plan projects using disciplined project management practices (scope confirmation, WBS, schedule, risk planning, onboarding).
Manage execution and controls: track progress, issues, changes, and dependencies; maintain project records in the project workspace for traceability.
Coordinate communications and reporting cadence; maintain deadline control for regulatory and client reporting obligations.
Manage vendors and subcontractors under defined procedures; ensure work plans and outputs follow required verification pathways.
Support digital field data collection and standardized reporting workflows; contribute to dashboards and evidence packs used for program and project visibility.
Prepare deliverables and ensure they are ready for check/review with project director and/or subject matter expert approval prior to external use.
Escalate risks and deviations early using leading indicators and agreed thresholds to support ‘no surprises’ delivery.
Close out projects with complete documentation, lessons learned, and handoff as required

What you will bring to the team:

Demonstrated experience in leading environmental field data collection, soil & groundwater investigations, and technical report preparation programs.
Ability to manage scope, schedule, cost, and risk with a structured approach.
Strong coordination skills across field/office resources, and multi-disciplinary technical teams.
Clear written and verbal communication skills; capable of producing and managing recurring reporting deliverables.
Ownership and follow-through on commitments
Strong attention to detail
Effective communication with technical and non-technical audiences
Collaborative relationships with clients and team members.
Leadership potential and a desire to grow into larger project management responsibilities
A balance of technical problem-solving with business and project objectives.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Geological, Geotechnical, Environmental, or Mining Engineering, or related field
Approximately 5+ years of technical experience in environmental remediation and site assessments, report writing, data management & interpretation, project coordination, and managing clients.
Project management experience is required beyond day-to-day task management (e.g., defining project scope/objectives, establishing and monitoring budgets, allocating resources, anticipating/mitigating risks).
Understanding of project management principles and methodologies required
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines required.
Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills required.
Prior experience coordinating projects, task teams, and technical work packages required
Exposure to project budgeting, scheduling, forecasting, or client management preferred
Exposure to project management systems such as project accounting software (e.g., BST, Deltek, etc.), MS Project, and/or Primavera P6 preferred,
Experience in remediation and reclamation of legacy mine sites preferred.
CERCLA, RCRA, and/or state-led remediation program experience a plus.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification desired
MSHA 24-hour New Miner training desired, but not required
Ability and willingness to travel to client meetings is required
PE a plus, but not required

jobs.title: Environmental, Health and Safety Manager – Sanford Advanced Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Career Area

Environmental Health and Safety

Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Caterpillar is developing a new advanced manufacturing campus in Sanford, North Carolina, to expand production capacity for compact track loaders and telehandlers. The modern, technology-enabled operation is expected to incorporate automation, robotics, digital production systems and integrated logistics capabilities to enhance safety, quality and operational performance. Employees will help build the products our customers rely on while developing skills in advanced manufacturing and supporting the continued growth of Caterpillar’s Cat Compact℠ business.

Job Summary

The Environmental, Health and Safety Manager will provide site-level EHS leadership for a new advanced manufacturing facility, helping the site launch safely and build strong operating discipline from the beginning. This leader will be involved from construction planning through startup and stable production. Early priorities will include contractor evaluation related to safety, safety training, contractor safety program adherence, construction risk, site controls and readiness.

This role supports Caterpillar’s Safety Driven culture, where safety is not a checklist or a set of procedures. It requires an EHS leader who can lead through ambiguity, influence project and operations leaders, work directly with contractors and employees, and build a safety culture where safe behavior is coached, expected and reinforced in the flow of daily work.

What You Will Do

Lead EHS execution for a new advanced manufacturing site from construction planning through startup.
Set clear construction-phase safety expectations for contractors, project teams and site leaders, including orientation, site access, work planning, hazard controls, inspections and corrective actions.
Build practical EHS programs, training, audits, reporting routines and risk-reduction processes that support Caterpillar standards, legal requirements and local operating needs.
Partner with construction, facilities, operations, engineering, maintenance, security, human resources, suppliers, contractors and system integrators to identify risks early and resolve issues quickly.
Support safe implementation of advanced manufacturing systems, automated material movement, connected equipment, robotics, energy systems, utilities and production processes.
Establish leader routines for hazard identification, risk assessment, contractor safety, incident response, corrective actions and emergency preparedness.
Use EHS data, leading indicators, inspections, observations, incident trends and audit findings to guide decisions and focus resources where risk is highest.
Provide leadership for environmental compliance, waste management, chemical management, air, water, stormwater, permitting and sustainability-related programs.
Coach leaders and employees, using field observations, feedback, leader routines and follow-up to reinforce safe decisions during construction and startup.

What You Will Have

Environmental Health and Safety Policy Compliance:
Knowledge of environmental, health and safety policies, standards, procedures and legal requirements; ability to lead programs that protect employees, contractors, visitors in a manufacturing environment.

Risk Management:
Knowledge of tools, approaches and practices for identifying, assessing, controlling and monitoring operational, environmental, construction and occupational-health risks before they become incidents.

Decision Making and Critical Thinking:
Ability to analyze technical, operational and compliance data, evaluate alternatives, assess risk and make sound recommendations. Ability to manage multiple priorities while balancing safety, compliance, schedule, cost and operational impact.

Project Management:
Ability to plan, organize, monitor and deliver EHS-related projects, launch activities, corrective actions and readiness plans to scope, schedule and quality expectations. Ability to work with cross-functional teams.

Safety Culture Leadership:
Ability to influence how leaders, employees and contractors think about risk, speak up about hazards, correct unsafe conditions and make safe choices in daily work.

Top Candidates Will Also Have

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health and Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Manufacturing, Construction Management.
Relevant EHS professional certification, such as CSP, ASP, CHMM, CIH, OSHA 30, ISO 14001, ISO 45001 or a comparable credential.
Experience improving EHS performance through both practical processes and behavior-based safety approaches.
Experience supporting construction safety, contractor safety, facility startup, capital projects, commissioning or major operational change.
Experience identifying hazards, assessing risk, implementing controls, investigating incidents and tracking corrective actions.
Strong communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills.

What You Will Get

Launch a new advanced manufacturing operation and shape the EHS foundation from construction through start up.
Lead work that supports Caterpillar’s Safety Driven culture and reinforces that safety is how the work gets done.
Play a visible leadership role in shaping how a new site operates from day one.
Help implement practical EHS systems that support automation, advanced manufacturing, and safe production.

Additional Info

Location: Sanford, North Carolina
Work Arrangement: Onsite, five days per week. Locations may flex between temporary offices while transitioning to new facility.
Travel: High percentage of travel (50-75%) may be required at certain times during construction planning, supplier reviews, equipment installation, commissioning, startup and production ramp-up.
Schedule: This will be a demanding and very rewarding role. Selected candidate should have schedule flexibility to meet project requirements.
Relocation: US domestic relocation is available
Visa Sponsorship: Not available

Summary Pay Range

$128,470.00 - $192,710.00

Compensation and benefits offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, job level, market location, job-related knowledge, skills, individual performance and experience. Please note that salary is only one component of total compensation at Caterpillar.

Benefits

Subject to plan eligibility, terms, and guidelines. This is a summary list of benefits.

Medical, dental, and vision benefits*
Paid time off plan (Vacation, Holidays, Volunteer, etc.)*
401(k) savings plans*
Health Savings Account (HSA)*
Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs)*
Health Lifestyle Programs*
Employee Assistance Program*
Voluntary Benefits and Employee Discounts*
Career Development*
Incentive bonus*
Disability benefits
Life Insurance
Parental leave
Adoption benefits
Tuition Reimbursement
These benefits also apply to part-time employees

This position requires working onsite five days a week.

Relocation is available for this position.

Visa Sponsorship is not available for this position.

October 5, 2026 - October 18, 2026

Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:

Posted Date 9/14/2026

Description

The City of Gresham is seeking a motivated and technically savvy Geographic Information System (GIS) Analyst to join our Enterprise GIS Team as a member of the City’s Information Technology Department. We are looking for an experienced self-starter with a passion for GIS, data integrity, process improvement, workflow automation, and support of new GIS technology. This position reports to the GIS Manager and serves city staff and the community alongside two GIS Analyst Seniors and a GIS Technician Senior. This role will support GIS projects and initiatives aligned with our Geospatial Strategy with a primary focus on data management, data analysis, automating workflows, and project management. If you love working with data, applying GIS tools in innovative ways to overcome technological hurdles, and helping others, you will thrive in this position that supports city staff and the community.

As Oregon's fourth-largest city, Gresham is a welcoming community of hard-working people where tradition and heritage meet innovation and opportunity. Gresham is a dynamic and rapidly growing city where families and businesses have a mutual desire and drive to thrive. City of Gresham employees care deeply about the community they serve and go 'one step beyond' to deliver services in collaborative, inventive, practical, and nimble ways. Our work is challenging, fast-paced and rewarding.

We believe that to deliver the highest level of service to all Gresham community members, it is crucial we employ a diverse workforce, foster an inclusive working environment, and ensure our policies and systems result in equitable outcomes. The City seeks candidates who will support these values by continuously incorporating equity in their daily work and actively contributing to a workplace culture that respects unique viewpoints, life experiences and cultural perspectives. Come build the future with us.

Position Description

What you will get to do

Create and manage data, information and documentation

Create, update, and maintain data and perform quality assurance processes to maintain integrity of data.
Develop and maintain datasets including database design, modeling, metadata, and integration in response to staff requests and project requirements.
Create and document procedures for business workflows, new datasets, and tools.

Data Analysis

Produce high quality maps, dashboards, and reports from analysis of the most complex nature.
Provide assistance and support to staff regarding spatial analysis and tool sets.
Utilize aerial imagery for raster analytics and LiDAR data for 3D analysis.

Process Automation

Develop custom scripts and applications to automate data collection, maintenance of geospatial datasets, and data analyses.
Perform spatial and non-spatial data extractions, transformation and loading processes, and analysis.

GIS Project Management

Work with internal and external stakeholders to understand their spatial and non-spatial data and analysis needs.
Facilitate project team meetings and manage the planning and implementation of small to medium sized GIS projects.
Determine business objectives, define scope, detail requirements, manage change, and help implement solutions.
Create a variety of information products including digital or paper maps, web maps, web apps, and mobile tools using cartographic, visualization and information management processes and standards.

Current or Upcoming Projects

Migrate existing water utility geospatial data to Esri’s Utility Network.
Implementation of ArcGIS Image Server to support raster analytics.
Development of a historic imagery tracker.
Development of an oriented imagery database.
Note: this is not an exhaustive list.

Coaching and Training

Review and monitor work for accuracy and content; evaluate projects, activities, and processes.
Train staff on new software solutions and/or workflows.
Assist with training staff on geoprocessing tasks and tools.
Train and make presentations to internal users.

Technical Support

Assist in resolving and troubleshooting GIS-related problems and requests.
Assist in installing and testing new GIS software.

Qualities we are looking for

Establish and maintain proactive, positive working relationships with internal and external customers and collaborate across diverse departments, stakeholders, and within the Enterprise GIS Team.
An engaged team member who contributes to team meetings by listening, observing and contributing information from current and past experiences.
An effective leader to create agendas and provide structure in meetings with vendors, the team, and others.
A natural curiosity and ability to independently research answers/solve problems.
Gracefully handle change, challenges, and multiple concurrent tasks.
We are seeking individuals who are not only experienced but also deeply passionate about GIS.
Ability to communicate effectively, transparently, and in a timely fashion.
Ability to express complex technical topics and issues to numerous audience types.
Proactively learn and implement new technology.
Strong prioritization skills.
Elevated skillset for providing and accepting assistance and feedback.
Exercise discretion in confidential and sensitive matters.
Provide effective motivation, coordination, and evaluation of others.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in geography, environmental studies, computer science, engineering, GIS, or related field.
One (1) to three (3) years of professional experience operating GIS using Esri’s software suite or related software, performing spatial analyses, creating and using spatial analytic tools, and leading project(s), or related work.

Any combination of qualifying education, training, and experience that meets the minimum requirements will be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

GISP Certification.
Experience with Python and/or other scripting and programming languages.
Experience with FME and/or Esri’s Data Interoperability extension.
Experience with raster and LiDAR analytics.

STV is seeking an experienced Geospatial Manager to help lead and grow our survey, reality capture, and digital delivery capabilities across Texas. This opportunity will be based primarily in Frisco, Texas, there the flexibility for it to be in any STV Texas office and offers the chance to manage high-impact infrastructure work, guide technical teams, and shape how high-quality project data is captured, processed, and delivered.

Why STV?
You will join a collaborative team that is investing in the future infrastructure delivery—combining survey expertise, reality capture, automation, and digital tools to deliver better data, faster for our clients.

Manage and guide UAV/UAS, laser scanning, mobile mapping, LiDAR, GNSS, and reality capture efforts for transportation, utility, municipal, construction, and infrastructure projects.

Develop accurate digital deliverables, including point clouds, orthomosaics, terrain models, surface models, existing conditions models, utility mapping, and 3D reality capture datasets.
